review_text: Many good sea food restaurants in the borough, but this one has the old fashioned clam shack feel.  An excellent clam chowder to start (I like the New England over the Manhattan) but the must-have here is the red sauce, especially the hot version.  Over the fried calamari, it is first rate.  The hot is hot enough to build a little sweat without burning the taste buds.  Real flavor. The medium is equally as good but I love food with the extra kick.  The downside..soda's are seriously overpriced since they still serve the little splits (and have been since I was a teen going there) and you will need a couple to wash down the sauce.  Open late, it was my comfort food stop when I went back and forth to Brooklyn when my Dad was ill.  (calamari in hot sauce as comfort food???? Yep!)

An old-style, no frills clam bar right on Sheepshead Bay. The best thing on the menu is their steamers - year round b/c they have their own farm. 99 times out of 100 the steamers are juicy, fresh, and absolutely delicious. I also love their calamari with hot sauce, scungilli, baked clams, linguine w/white clam sauce, and lobster bisque. the restaurant is not classy, the waitresses are a bit rough around the edges, and the silverware can always use an extra wash, but this place is still one of my favorite local eats.

You know that any place that can get away with looking like a high school cafeteria is doing something right. Randazzo's has the best steamers I've ever had and I grew up on them. They were absolutely delicious! My boyfriend tried them for the first time and agreed wholeheartedly. I'm a bit of a purist when it comes to lobster bisque, so I was a teensy bit put off by the chunks of potato and celery in my soup, but the flavor of the large pieces of lobster were so delicious that all was forgiven. The bisque definitely made my top 5.

This place serves drinks out of plastic cups, bright lights and brings water for the table in a plastic pitcher; but it was pretty good seafood for the area.  We started with the steamers, which we sandy, but that's to be expected.  We then shared the spicy crab corn chowder soup, it was good, but no Maryland Crab soup.  I had the fried calamari with medium sauce, it was tasty, but I do wish I had ordered the hot sauce since the medium wasn't spicy for me.  The sauce was chunky and tasty.  My mom ordered the lobster broiled, it was OK....supposed to come with a salad (but she didn't get it). My boyfriend ordered the seafood fra diablo over linguine, which was good.  The sauce was very liquidity but the shrimps, clams and mussels were good.  

After all was sad and down...this wasn't the best clam bar I've been too and we did spend over 80 dollars for three people, but I might go back, the calamari was the best choice.

I go here at least once a month with my Dad, and I don't know what I'd do without it.  Their steamers are huge and juicy, and the pasta with lobster sauce is off the chain, with big, meaty chunks of lobster.  Oh, and of course, raw oysters and clams on the half-shell.

The place is not fancy,... hell they serve you water in a large plastic pitcher with some plastic cups, but that is the beauty of it. It is a simple good seafood place. As long as you are dressed well enough to be on the street you are dressed well enough to go to Randazzo's. 

The service is good, though they won't take any attitude from you (and are very likely to give you some). They food is excellent as long as you don't expect high class presentation. The fried zucchini is always a treat with some calamari with hot sauce. 

Really there isn't much to add that hasn't been said. Go get some food at Randazzo's and then take a walk over to the boardwalk to watch the weekly fireworks in the summer on a Friday night. If that isn't your thing take a walk to a desert place further down Emmons avenue and just watch the people. It is hard not to have a good time.

Everyone seems to be right on about this place. I just cant believe no one is raving about the stuffed shrimp or the Scungilli with hot sauce. Steamers like everyone said is the best ever and there is nothing like a dozen little necks to suck down before I really start to eat all of Randazzo's  seafood glory ( and hard little biscuit on the plate too drenched in sauce). Man Im hungry! This website is killing me!

I was surprised their steamers were so big. I remember little necks being small and sweet, even the necks tender. Not these, these were large and a bit tough. My gf had the soft shell crab sandwich was to die for, and both types of clam chowders were delicious. It's a no frills place, old school clam bar house. They even served chilled red wine !!! :D How funny. 
After trying to explain to my friend how yelp works, there on the counter was a placard saying they had been yelped and displaying their 5 star review! Yelp, much like big brother is everywhere!
Sadly, 3000 miles did not make for better steamers, but what the heck!
4 stars for the rest of the food. And you can't but a price on the friendliness of these folks. Makes me wonder ...... where the rest of the country went wrong.

I got the fried calamari and loved it. I ordered a side of the hot sauce and it   was very tasty, not hot to me. I also had the medium sauce and it was not nearly as good as the hot version. Fried yet digestible, this is a Brooklyn treasure. We waited 20 min to get our table for 4 seated, but they did not rush us out at the end. Tiny sodas, but the pitcher of water helped.

I would go back!

One of the few places where you can find native Brooklynites dining en masse. Pauly the owner being the opitimy of a native "Goodfella" with his Tony Manero hairstyle, over golding and Brooklynese dialect.

Except for the clams on the half the food is pretty mediocre.  Most of the shellfish is over steamed in way too much fresh water.  Even the fried food doesn't hold much flavor.  The sauces are okay. It's a shame because I remember when Randazzo's and a place called Joe's ruled Emmons Avenue.  You're pretty much going for the history and not the culinary.

Fun great place for Italian/Seafood 

Amazing place that has a special wonk quality. 

Seafood is fresh and amazing
Sauces are delicous 

Recommend 
Fra Diavolo (Sauce with the lobster is amazing)
Lobster Bisque - amazing 
Oyster/Clams - nice renditions 

Worth the headache of Sheepshead Bay traffic

Went to Randazzo's this weekend with two friends after having a serious clams and oysters craving..

The place is super casual, very nice, and lots of people there at all times..

Raw Cherry Hill Clams - delicious

The raw oysters were okay.. if you are a true oyster fanatic, this is not the place to go... but my friend Katy who is a casual oyster eater thought they were quite tasty..

Baked Clams were not very good, too much bread, not much flavor.. we also got fried oysters and it was too much bread and not enough oyster flavor...

If you really want seafood, i would go into the city and eat at Schaffer's Oyster Bar or Aquagrill..

I have been going to this place since I was a little tiny person. Service is just serviceable, so order everything you might possibly want all at once at the beginning, including drinks. (Though it's completely reasonable to yell for your waitress across the restaurant when you're a regular.) It's very much a down-and-dirty locals place.

Their truly special menu items:
The Sauce (comes in medium or hot; sometimes the medium is oppressive and sometimes the hot tastes like medium, but the flavor behind the heat is always great) on anything,
The lobster bisque (not insanely heavy on the seafood chunks but the flavor is absolutely perfect)
The fried shrimp (in The Sauce.. I love the bread that comes with)
The fried calamari (always crisp, never rubbery)
The scallop sandwich (plain but nicely cooked)

Walk-up service in the summer is the best. I wouldn't order the oysters any other way.

Right next door to THE Loehmann's and I never do one without the other. Also not far from the walkway to Manhattan Beach, which has the most bizarre mish-mash of different house styles you will ever see in your life.

The raw bar is ok, the food is ok. Our own waitress was actually wonderful - if you ever go, she's the only young female waitress that is pretty. Went there for father's day and braved the rainstorm to make it across town to eat there. When they brought out raw oysters and clams, the water that was in them that they use to clean them spilled on my mother and her purse. My mother shrieked from the ice water and the server who brought them yelled at my mother to "relax - it's only water". She didn't even offer a napkin to wipe or even bother to apologize, she shook her head and walked away. I was appalled at that and on top of that the average price of a dish is $18.95!! We ordered over $145 worth of food (there were 6 of us) and not once did anyone come to give napkins or an apology. We had to ask for napkins to clean my mother up. So after we received all our dishes we notified our waitress our displeasure and she profusely apologized on behalf of the lady who spilled the water on my mother. If you're on the look out - it's the older fat lady with the dark (dye-job) short boy cut hair. She offered to notify the owner who came over and just simply said "Sorry" - not sincerely and he didn't even offer a discount on the bill or at least free dessert. He just said "sorry" and walked away. Seriously, you should walk away from a dining experience with an overall satisfaction at paying what you pay given today's economy, but I can honestly I would never eat there again, the food was average and the disrespect to my mother was unacceptable. I'm tired of NY restaurants that are willing to sacrifice service and offer moderate food. Competition is tough, gas prices are on the rise, offer us something to be satisfied about!

The decor is pretty cheap so if you want something casual - it's as casual as you can get. The cherry stone clams are pretty small compared to other establishments in the city and the prices are pretty high for the neighborhood.

It was a raining day; the New England clam chowder was good (I like Whole Food's also if there's not so much freaking sand inside). The crab in the $16 soft shell crab sandwich is big, comes with claws but nothing special. The lobster pasta is like other people said: lots of lobster meat but the sauce is not too good. The waitress forgot the fried calamari which people rave about. This place does remind me Tony's Clam Shop in Quincy, MA.

Calamari are real good especiall the sauce, which is real thick.
Lobster sauce w/ pasta is the best, though I would stay away from the clam sauce.

This place is always the first to pop into my head if I thinking of a place to go to and splurge a bit.  The first time I went I was brought there by some friends. We split 2 lobsters, crab legs, baked clams, raw clams, and raw oysters between 3 people.  The price came out to about $40 a person, tip included.  The food was delicious though in my opinion. I would love to go back and try other things if I had the money =P

Randazzo's is a mainstay on Emmons Ave in Sheepshead Bay.

This is an excerpt of the review posted on our site:
AOL's City's Best Guide to New York gave top honors to Randazzo's Clam Bar (2023 Emmon's Ave.) in its seafood category.

The neighborhood staple beat out such elite eateries as Le Bernardin and the Aquagrill in Manhattan, as well as other sea critter cookers around the city. Around since the 1920s, Randazzo's is a relic of a waterfront that was once lined with world-class seafood restaurants, so if you haven't already, make sure you hit it up at least once before it's turned into a condo.

There shrimp and fried calamari platter with sauce of your choice is aces and the other food is overall pretty good, better to take on the run VERY crowded and the fellow customers can be VERY rude. This is a pricey place as well (worth it to me).

god, i really wanted to like this place.

we made a point of trying all the stuff people rave about - the lobster bisque, the calamari with hot sauce, and the shrimp fra diavolo.  all were good, but not really memorable.  the seafood they used was fresh.

we also tried the pasta with lobster sauce, which i found appalling.  the lobster was clearly overcooked and overly fishy.  i couldn't believe they charged me $20 for that crap.

i wouldn't recommend coming here unless you are in the neighborhood and plan to go for the three things everyone mentions... and i certainly wouldn't recommend making the trek just to try this place.

I always find myself coming here when I want some clams or calamari. Never had any complaints. I went a couple of weeks ago and downed a dozen of their oysters. It's a big deal for me because I could of sworn I was
allergic to seafood. Let me correct that statement. I am allergic to shrimp and crabs. But while on vacation,  I ate scallops and had the calamari with a lobster aioli on the side without incident so now it's like a whole new world for me! 

Wish me luck because I'm having a lobster this weekend!

Oh Randazzo's, what the hell happened on Tuesday?  I haven't been here in years but my overwhelming last memory of the place is my friend and I wearing our bibs and digging into delicious lobster.  This time, though, the lobster was tough, overcooked and likely had been frozen.  Pretty blech.  The only reason it's getting 3 stars instead of 1 or 2 is because of previous positive experiences here and the fact that my friend enjoyed his fried scallops.

Anyone who gives this place less than 4 stars doesn"t know seafood. You don't judge this place for its chicken fingers -- go to KFC for that. This is the best clambar in the world. That's right people its a clambar and the most amazing one at that. I've been going here for over 20 years and it doesn't get any better than this. This is not the place you go to impress your new hot girlfriend or to get your hiney powdered. This is a down to earth, loud, blue collar restaurant where you get great fresh seafood at a good price. Yes, the menu is limited and that is precisely why everything is so fresh -- its something called specializing. 
Food in order of favorite:
              1.clams
              2. calamari (w/ medium sauce)
              3. scungilli
              4.lobster

Sorry, the chicken fingers didn't make the list -- my 3 yr old son will have to review them since I never tried them. He uses the word tummy and says he likes them for his tummy and that they are yummy but then again I think they are on the menu for children.

It's a small crowded place and not much to look at, but the food is great. I had the Lobster Bisque (Amazing!) and the Shrimp Scampi. It's pricey, but the portions are pretty big. Don't expect a quiet meal. Waiters yell orders to the cook across the room. It's not a romantic atmosphere, but you'll go home full and happy (albeit less money in your pocket).  I only wish they had dessert.
Low quality ingredients and high prices.  Cooking is as retro as it gets.  Service gruff old New York style.  I feel sick about what I was charged for a very unenjoyable meal here.

This place is famous for seafood. Expect to wait awhile on the weekends for a table.

After waiting for about half an hour for a table, I expected fantastic food. The food is nothing to be excited over. Standard seafood.

Say what you want about Randazzo's, but I love it.  Allow me to summarize:

1.) Its a very good neighborhood place.  Don't go expecting a fancy restaurant with amazing food, and you should enjoy it.

2.) Obviously there's no dress code, so don't be an idiot and dress up.

3.) The fried calamari is amazing. Don't miss it; order it without a biscuit and you'll get a little extra calamari.

4.) Their sauce is very interesting.  It works with the seafood, but not so much with the pasta.  Get it hot, you won't regret it.

5.) If you are planning on ordering something other than seafood, matter of fact don't bother coming.  

6.) Its noisy and staff and regulars aren't afraid to yell across the restaurant.  Get used to it.


If you don't like you're hearing so far, don't go.  Now with all of that said, the food is very good in a homestyle way.  They definitely know how to cook seafood, their portions are very big for the main courses (calamari orders are a little small, hence the biscuit comment), and it is fairly pricey.  But there's a reason why they are ranked among the best seafood in the city.  Just get used to the big thurmoses of water they drop off, the old-Brooklyn waitstaff and everything else that I couldn't completely list if I tried.  Its part of the experience.

first off i love the marina atmosphere and the strip this clam bar is on. i ate outdoors because it is so pretty on that strip and good for people watching and to enjoy the nice weather. the food was amazing. the crab cake sandwich and the the little necks baked clams were sooo yummy! love it and it smells great all around it! best part is you can enjoy a nice beer as well. the wait staff is great.. i had a  blonde lady with a real thick brooklyn accent... mid 30's maybe.. tall i forgot her name she was so helpful and real cool.  she made sure we took our time hence the long wait for others for outdoor seating. and she even let us smoke outside which was prohibitied... would love to go again!

Wow. 

I feel really sorry for writing this review. I haven't eaten at Randazzo's in nearly 20 years. The last time I was there was as a kid with my father and I had a fond memory of eating whatever it was. With the recent news that the owner of Randazzo's passed away I decided to head on over to have some Calamari.

My friend and I ordered Mozzarella Sticks and Fried Calamari to share, he got the New England Clam Chowder and I got a half order of Linguine in Marinara.

I'm sad to say that I was completely and utterly underwhelmed and unsatisfied. The amount of Calamari you get for an 11$ dish is....paltry. For 11 bucks I expect a dish big enough to split between two people but there was barley enough there for HALF a person. The biscuit that came with the calamari was hard, toasted and soggy all at the same time. I wasn't too impressed with the Mozzarella Sticks either. I tasted more crust then cheese. The Linguine was ok, but the Marinara was pretty bland. The sauce just didn't come alive in my mouth like I expect it too!

Finally, they have the gall to charge $1.50 for a 10oz bottle of soda. What the hell? They can't at least serve a standard 20oz bottle? Even a CAN of soda is 12oz!

*Sigh* I'm so disappointed I'm not really sure what to say. I came in expecting way too much I guess, but for a Brooklyn Legend you SHOULD expect a lot. 

If you want a good plate of Fried Calamari you'd be better off going to Jordans Lobster Dock or Prima Pasta. Frankly you'd be better off ordering a plate of Calamari and Pasta from your local pizzeria!

I used to come here as a kid, so I have nostalgic memories here.

A few months ago I went to NYC, to work on a few music videos. Since I was given a car, I HAD to make a necessary trip here.

It looked exactly the same, and even the staff did too (lol?). It reminds me of Las Vegas. Well, 70's Vegas. The lights outside are a bit over whelming. You'll soon forget about the decor, and start stuffing your face.

Service here is prompt, and to the point. Just how I like it.

We shared a bunch of random clams and oysters. C'est tres magnificent!!! For my main entree, I had the stuffed lobster. I'm not a big fan of lobster. I actually don't care for lobster at all. This lobster made me care. It was stuffed with shrimp, crab, and it was mixed with some sort of stuffing. My taste buds were in heaven. I can't tell you how the flavors twirled in my mouth, and left me in a surreal state. 

Work covered the bill, so I have no idea how much it was. I know it wasn't cheap.

It's next to the original Roll N Roaster!!!!

A true staple of the Sheepshead Bay area.  Randazzo's has been frequented since I was at the age of 10.  The restaurant offerings are well priced, high quality seafood in a low key family oriented atmosphere.  It's not surprising that Randazzo's has lasted for so many years, with frequent wait times due to the excessive local patronage that returns to sample the offerings.

The service:  Efficient, Friendly, and Welcoming!  The waitresses that work at Randazzo's have been there anywhere from 5 to 10 years.  Needless to say, the service is top notch as it's been embedded as a craft, rather than a job.

The atmosphere:  Old School and lively!  With furniture going back to the 1970's, the food is the main attraction at Randazzo's.  The patrons that frequent Randazzo's are locals, while constantly returning as the food never gets old.  Walking into Randazzo's is similar to walking into a Sheepshead Bay hot spot, it's going to be rowdy, but everyone is generally very welcoming.  Needless to say, Randazzo's is the place to relax and be yourself.  There's not one bit of pretentious feel in the air.

The Food:  Top notch seafood at its very best!

Appetizers - 

Fresh Cherrystone Clams (1/2 Dozen): Fresh and buttery to the touch!  The slightly sweet and meaty composition of the Cherrystones were in full force during the clams' consumption.  The light use of lemon juice and cocktail sauce helped to elevate the freshness and meaty texture of the Cherrystones.  Furthermore, the Cherrystones tasted so fresh it appeared as though the clams were removed from the ocean to order.

New England Clam Chowder:  Although visually similar to most New England Clam Chowders, the taste is the ultimate dissemination of Randazzo's rendition.  At first taste, patrons will find that the buttery and savory flavors derived from the heavy cream and clams come to full force in this application.  The heartiness derived from the chowder is representative of a well executed version of this classic consumable.  Patrons will find the velvety texture of Chowder to work in conjunction with the mild firmness of the Clams used in the application.  Ultimately, the consumption of this Clam Chowder will allow patrons to fully understand its composition.  Through a well executed texture (for which it is not too liquidity or dense), the elements of the application works to stimulate the flavors derived from the heavy cream and spices.  Although the clam meat itself was slightly lacking on the plentiful side, the heart flavors stemming from the Clam Chowder are top notched and well renowned.

Fried Calamari: In lieu of the simplistic presentation which consisted of a heap of Calamari and a small container of Mariniara, the taste and boldness derived from the application was exquisite.  The textural contrast between the crispy peripheral complemented the smooth and soft nature of the Calamari.  The taste too complimented the textural composition of the application.  Light hints of salt and garlic played well in both taste and aromatics of the application.  Patrons ordering the Fried Calamari will find that the simplistic nature but bold taste and texture of the Calamari will render second orders.

Entrees:

Shrimp Fra Diavolo:  Extra Large Shrimp, Massive Bed of Linguine, Tons of Garlic, Medium Hot Sauce.  4 simple components, endless array of robust and captivating flavors.  What needs to be emphasized about Randazzo's Shrimp Fra Diavolo is old school presentation of the dish.  The Linguine is cooked in salted water, propped with pan fried shrimp (sauteed with Garlic), and doused with Medium Hot Sauce.  No fancy cooking the pasta with the sauce at Randazzo's, it's old school presentation.  Although the Shrimp and Pasta were "slightly" overcooked, the abundant amount of Extra Virgin Olive Oil rendered from the Medium Hot Sauce helped to save the dish.  Patrons will find that the hearty and thick composition of the Tomato Sauce was the main component in bringing together the ingredients of the application.  With each additional bite, the heightened level of spiciness helps to deliver the garlic and oregano flavors in the dish.  Patrons will find the Shrimp Fra Diavolo application to be a true comfort food!

Needless to say, when in Sheepshead Bay and in desperate need for a Seafood Fix, head to Randazzo's!

My new happy place!

No reservations, no fancy attire, and no hoity toity attitude. This 4th-generation family-owned clam bar is Brooklyn's equivalent to the New England clam shack. There's an organized buzz of activity, and the hum of this well-oiled machinery is punctuated by calls for orders.  

("LEGS! I NEED SOME HOT LEGS!")

This is one of the few places outside of New England I've seen with steamers on the menu.  They're a little pricier than up the coast, but every single steamer in the basket was large, meaty, and opened. The "famous" Randazzo sauce is actually deserving of its notoriety -- it's so good, it's worth getting the calamari appetizer (steamed), just to have a means to deliver the sauce to your belly! Likewise, every pasta dish with this sauce is an equally fantastic means of sauce delivery, plus the generous heaping of seafood will just about put you over the edge to actual bliss. If ordering any dish with a pink sauce, be forewarned that you'll actually be getting more of a garlic and butter sauce rather than a vodka sauce (my companion was a bit disappointed by this). We watched plate after plate of heaping amounts of food come out, loaded with quality items.  No hint of fishiness anywhere and the clams from the raw bar were perfectly briny. After stuffing ourselves, we still had leftovers for another full meal!  

Be prepared for a line on Friday and Saturday nights, but the wait goes by quick as food service is brisk without making you feel rushed. Wine is of the airline bottled variety, and there's also a long diner-type counter you can eat at while watching the bustle of the fry and raw bar stations.

Get calamari and mussels.  

Right by the Sheepshead Bay.  Randazzo is an Italian-owned at-home seafood restaurant.  The best dish I had here was Zuppa di Mussels in Red Sauce!  Omg, that was so tasty. The sauce is just so tasty.  It's got nice flavor of tomato and fresh garlic.  Dip your bread in the sauce, and that's the best.  And, their calamari is good.  You get to pick how you would like it , either soft or hard.  Order soft, it never goes wrong.  

On the other hand, their pastas were not good...  The pastas were just overcooked.  I recommend ordering a few dishes and share with your people because the portion is large.

One more.  My friend ordered some little necks and cherry stones.  She said the awful raw flavor lasted so long and could not help chewing a gum to get rid of it...  I didn't try them because I could smell it.  It was not raw but definitely needed lots of squeezes of lemon.

A tried and true Brooklyn spot at heart. I love summer time by the bay, getting a number and waiting on line for a table inside or a bench outside for some clams and oysters on half shell. 

A good mix of people: families, lovers and friends meet and mingle over seafood and pasta. 

My favorite is when they have Steamers in season. Really big in size, and delicious dipped in the melted butter.

Hands down the BEST Clamari in the world and Ohhhhh my goodness the sauce that comes with it and the hard garlic roll.. Truly the 8th wonder of the world.. I love Randazzos and you will too, no doubt.

Awesome seafood restaurant! By the amount of customers they get everyday you know their stuff are fresh. The calamari hands down the freshest with delicious red sauce slapped with a thick piece of garlic toast on the side. After eating the calamari, the bread is soaked with the red sauce and tastes sooo good!!! It made me lick the plate cause it's that good. Stuffing too, after eating a plate of that and a plate of fresh mussels also with it's famous red spicy tomato sauce I was pretty much full and set for my day after biking long miles around the area. Was really tempting on getting a bowl of seafood pasta but already fed good with the two appertiser dishes so definitly going back again to try a large size of the pasta entree they have. I still dream about the sauce... Hmm...

this is one of those places where you wish they were closer to where you live. I love this place! every time i go, i always get the same thing because i know it's delicious and i don't go often so by the time i go, i crave the same thing once again. the Fri Diavlo. I am probably spelling it wrong, but point is, it;s delicous and the portion is nice so i always just split it with my boyfriend. I've tasted other things on occasion when I have gone with friends and they ordered something. No matter what it is, it has been delicious :)

Once a year we go back to Brooklyn and we have a path of restaurants that we go to. Randazzos is near the top of this list. 

A Brooklyn tradition, not just Brooklyn. Randazzos sits on Sheepshead Bay, where you can hang by the docks and see the fishing boats come in and out. 

Between the ages of 14 and 17 my friends and I would get to the docks around 5am and we would fish right off the docks. We always caught a few but I always threw them back. I never felt comfortable eating them right there, swimming in the gas and oil filled bay. 

Anyway on to the review. 

You cannot get fresher tastier seafood than this. The cherry stones are sweet and delicious the oysters are the best. 

The fried calamari is the crispiest and chewiest at the same time and the sauce is slow cooked to perfection with the medium spice being just right. 

If you like Clam chowder this is the place for you, either white or red you cannot go wrong. 

I have been eating here for many years and anytime I go to New York I always make trip to Sheepshead Bay fro the seafood and head right to Randazzos. 

Cannot wait to return
Everything here is good! Their lobster randazzo is amazing. Their calamari, steamers, and clam chowder (both white and red) are SO good!

Not a hot spot at all. Went there as a back up cuz red lobster was jammed packed.  Sis was there before and she recommended it cuz we all wanted seafood. It's a nice a location because u can see the water but the food wasn't all that for the price they charged. They are not an upscale place so they have no business to b over charging. Small plate of calamari $10, 1 soda not even size of can is $1.50, regular lipton tea $2. Raw oysters were not fresh, all were so small and skinny. Choices limited so only got pasta. A lobster tail w/baked potato is $45.  Hell no! Definitely will not go there again. Oh by the way, just for a family of 6 who ordered 3 entrees and some appetizers and split it, the bill was close to $175. Oh yea, soup tasted like it came straight from the can. For $5 a bowl, I can buy 4 cans for $5 at Pathmark. Just not cool!

A failed attempt at eating at Totonno's in Coney Island on a foggy Saturday night in April[1] was salvaged by a wrong turn on Belt Pkwy that landed us on Sheepshead Bay, on the arms of Randazzo's Clam Bar.

I like the old school, relaxed vibe of this place: the gritty neon lights, the formica tables, the pale green plastic covering the long eating counter, the loud, familial tone with which the owner and the chef would address patrons, the mixed clientele.

We got the combo platter of scungilli, mussels, shrimp, and calamari. The scungilli were a great surprise: nice and tender, and as flavorful as they come. The mussels, which were steamed, were on the small size and not that good. The shrimps, which were fried without batter, were nice and plump. The calamari were excellent: perfectly fried, with the kind of texture and consistency I like.

We then had a plate of steamers. These babies were HUGE! The biggest ones I've ever had. They were tender and buttery, packed with flavor. Moreover, the serving was more than enough for two people.

Our waitress was nice and attentive. 

There were quite a few faux pas, however:
We weren't given any water, nor knives. Knives would have been useful with the huge steamers. Beer was served in plastic cups. No bread on the table. The combo came with a piece of soggy bread in the middle that was rock hard[2]. The marinara sauce, although very tasty, was too mild. And we even got the hot one!

A shared combo (scungilli, mussels, calamari, and shrimp), plus a generous serving of steamers, two Becks, and tips came to $30/each. Not cheap, considering they serve you drinks in plastic cups, but not too bad either.

Perhaps next time, once the outdoor dining area is open, I'll try the broiled lobster stuffed with shrimp and crab meat that was looking at me amorously from the table to my right...
-------------------------------------------------
[1] It was closed. At 9 PM. WTF?!

[2] Really, what was the purpose of this piece of bread?

Randazzo's Clam Bar has been around for over 40 years so it definitely has to have street cred.

Easter Sunday early dinner.  Place was packed.  Waited for about 15 minutes.

What was ordered.

- Lobster Bisque, okay but could be better.
- New England Clam Chowder, very good.
- Dozen Raw Little Neck Clams, good, fresh.
- Dozen Raw Cherry Stone clams, good, fresh.
- Dozen Raw Oysters, good, fresh.
- Zuppa di Mussels
- Fried Calamari, a little better than average, still too much batter for my liking.
- Spaghetti tossed with butter and garlic, ok.
- Baked Clams, very good

Didn't have steamers this evening.  Shucks!  Could have been the extra Yelp star.  Maybe next time.

NO, I didn't dine alone, there were 7 of us.  :)

As for decor, nothing fancy, old school mostly.
Parking can be a challenge, but luckily not for me, literally right in front of the resto.

Service was above average (experienced service staff who know what they are doing for sure!)

Overall the place was good, and since I can't say I am a fan, 3-stars goes to Randazzo's.  Probably would hit it again if I was in the Sheepshead Bay area, but not a place I would go out of my way to get to.

went there on a Saturday.. waited for about.. 15 minutes. the atmosphere was great, you can hear the chef, owner and the waiter shouting across the room to put an order. 
the food was awesome! the fresh clam was the best.. i tried both of the raw clams, little neck and cherry stone. i think the cherry stone was better. it was sweet and fresh. little neck was kind small. the oysters was okay.. fresh, but small as well. 
I'm so gonna go there again..

I have to admit, I didn't much care for my first visit to Randazzo's, the high prices and lousy service turned me off (the waitress slammed down my linguine so hard that clam sauce splashed on my blouse, and she didn't even apologize). I am glad that my husband convinced me to give it another shot. This time, we had a very nice, welcoming waitress who was attentive enough without being annoyingly fussy. 

We both had the lobster fradiavlo, and it was absolutely awesome. It's actually a lot more than lobster though. In addition to the whole cut lobster, there are a few mussels, a few clams and a couple of shrimp, over your choice of linguine or spaghetti in a  delicious spicy red sauce. It's messy as hell to crack lobster shells that are covered in tomato sauce, but it's delicious (they do give you a bib and wet naps, but it's still messy!). The wait was reasonable considering it was Saturday evening. Plain no frills bread, but it was nice and warm and sopped up the sauce just fine. As other reviewers have mentioned, the tiny soda bottles are a little annoying. 

It's not a very pretty place (a few changes like putting the Pepsi cooler out of sight would go a long way in improving the appearance), and I was disappointed that they didn't have outdoor tables, but the food was great and the service was nice. I am looking forward to returning to try their baked clams and some of their fried goodies (scallops, shrimp, oysters, clams, soft shell crabs, they have all that stuff).
If you have the misfortune of being stuck in South Brooklyn, at least make sure you get to Randazzo's to take advantage of their seafood dishes.  Place is great.

After having suffered the disappointment otherwise known as Jordan's Lobster Dock, I was wary of the seafood places in the area. However, I had a major craving for seafood and I was already in the area so I stopped in for a late lunch. I was happy to see there was waiter service, the place was a decent size, and there was a pretty large crowd inside even though it was 3:00. 

We got the fried calamari, lobster bisque, baked clams (Little Neck AND Cherry Stone, and crab cake. The lobster bisque was more of a chowder, the Little Neck clams were better than the Cherry Stone clams IMO, and the crab cake was dry, bland, and overcooked. You're probably wondering what about the fried calamari? Well, the waitress forgot to bring it out, which brings me to the quality of the service. 

I think there were two waitresses on duty at the time, but only one was taking orders. The other one just walked around, served a couple of dishes here and there. We had to wait about 15 minutes after we sat down before she came over to take our order. Then, at the end, she gave us the bill before we asked for it AND she totaled everything up including the fried calamari which she had completely forgotten about. 

All in all, this was another disappointment. I might stop in again for the baked Little Neck clams and finally try the fried calamari. Otherwise, I'm eating my seafood elsewhere.

Ladies and Gents-- I am officially a member of the "Yelp-Mile-High Club."

That's right, I'm writing this review 30,000 feet in the air on Virgin America.

Now down to business. Came here to grab a quick snack with the old man so he could revisit his childhood --he used to come here to get some clams as a kid. 

So we did. They were baked and amazing, Truly some of the best I've ever had. This place was so good and so cool I would take the subways all the way down to Sheapshead Bay next time in in NYC just to go back.

Everything looked good and the family style ambiance and service makes you feel at home. 

Lots of seating but I liked being up at the clam bar.
the waitress are awesome and badass here and the food is awesome flaky seafood goodness.  good solid sandwiches and big portions!

One of Brooklyn's best!   Randazzo's has been a landmark Sheepshead Bay restaurant for ages.   On my way to Philly from Long Island (via the Belt parkway aka The Belt) I decided to stop for a quick lunch and boy am I glad I did!

This iconic restaurant still looks and feels like the Brooklyn of my childhood, something so comforting about it's counter and table dining along with the prepping and deep frying right in front of the customers.

Must haves and had, New England Clam Chowder, dozen raw clams on the half shell served with horseradish and cocktail sauces, the freshest and "Best" fried calamari (or as said in Brooklyn, galamar) and fried zucchini sticks! The calamari is freshly cut, battered and fried at the counter and comes to your plate hot, fresh and soft, NOT chewy!  The fried zucchini sticks are delicious, a must have!  

The food is fresh, the servers are friendly and the prices are reasonable.   As this is one of the last restaurants left from the old days, I can only hope that it can survive the gentrification and change over in the area.
Classic Brooklyn southern Italian. Great chicken parm. Same great food as when I was kid growing up in Brooklyn.

My friends have been raving about this place for some time now, and I finally got to try it yesterday! 

Its a simple place, no frills, no airs...just seafood. We ordered the spicy crab corn chowder, dozen oysters, dozen little necks, and crab cake sammich. The corn chowder was delish, but not very spicy. The raw bar was fresh, a bit briny but thats ok...its extra flavour! The crab cake sandwhich comes in 2 patties so you can share easily. It was mostly lump crap smashed into a patty, not a whole lot of that crap filling to piece it together ---perfect! Oh...we also had fried calamari, but it was just OK...

My only disappointment is when you order a soda, its not a giant fountain soda, its a little glass coke bottle that I think barely quenches any thirst from eating all that seafood. So i think next time i'll just stick to the h2o.

Great old school place, simple and to the point.  They server a number of raw and italian american seafood dishes.  The service is quick and food is fresh.  The cherrystones on the half shell were ice cold and fresh and perfect on a hot summer day. The steamed and fried seafood like calamari or scungilli is served smothered with either medium or hot red sauce(not really that HOT).  But if you are looking for old time brooklyn seafood joint this is the place to go.

The main attraction is clearly the heaping plate of steamies -- meaty and engorged with steamy goodness. Don't be off-put by the sweepies (you'll know what I mean when you order them)--this is a delicacy, much like the French have escargot or the Japanese have poisonous blowfish. Bring the whole family.

Dysfunctional. If there were one word to describe this absolutely bonkers place, it would be 'dysfunctional.' Located on Emmons Avenue right on the Bay, it is surrounded by the amazing nightlife which only adds to hectic atmosphere of Randazzo's Clam Bar.

Upon entering the place, you notice a man that one can only inaptly assume is the maître d' -- a fairly large man with large sunglasses, most likely donning an incredible Hawaiian shirt of some sort. Sitting by the bar gives you front row seats to the whole operation -- and why the word 'dysfunctional' should be Randazzo's middle name. You can see the cooks shucking the mussels, and flouring your seafood as well you in the process. And you can see the waitresses carrying way too many plates in a space that only an anorexic runway model would feel comfortable in. This place is a contradiction enclosed within four walls, where disorder is order. 

While they don't claim that their seafood is fresh, there is a sign that clearly indicates otherwise -- "Fresh seafood is not cheap; cheap seafood is not fresh." I, however, must say that my fried clams did come out of a bag, and while it may not be seafood, that bread that came along with my clams were paradoxically hard as a rock and soggy like wet newspaper (it certainly tasted like wet newspaper). It isn't clear-cut how this place manages to service its patrons without evoking the chaos theory; however there is no doubt in my mind that the seafood, topped off with that amazing tomato sauce, is probably the best in the Brooklyn area. It's food without the pretentiousness - the best kind of food. Where there aren't twenty forks to eat that piece of delicious lobster.

 You may be tempted to get all the fried seafood, but I assure you that whatever you order will stand its own, fried or not. This place may be out of the way for many people but if you happen to be in the neighborhood for a movie, definitely stop by for some delicious food served by a wonderful staff.  Coincidentally, that same staff is as maladjusted as your spoiled cousin, however it's the same cousin everyone in the family just loves.

After a very long hot day of animal rescue we decided to sit outside at Randazzo's- location is perfect as I live right across the bay and can almost throw a rock and hit my roof! The waitress brought menus at once, I asked about the iced tea, thkfully she was truthful and said that it was lipton bottles- yuck! That was the best thing I can say, it went downhill fast.
 We ordered a bowl of spicy crab chowder and a lobster bisque for starters- fried zuchinni  and 1/2 spaghetti for aps
and then she took our menus away without ever getting our main course orders which I always decide on after I eat my first two courses.
 The spicy crab was laden with fresh crab meat, and corn, not overly spicy but decent. The lobster bisque was more of a chowder with NO Lobster to speak of upon pouring a few spoonfuls onto a plate and not finding any lobster pieces I asked the waitress if they forgot to add the lobster- (for a 10 dollar bowl served in a little plastic take out container I at least want a couple chunks of meat!) She asked if I would like to see the owner, I sad yes
 . A moment later she returned saying she would take back the bisque, but we couldn't have ANYTHING ELSE! And then she started glaring over at us whispering to other servers!
 In a few seconds the owner came out gold chains, bad hair and a wild look in his eye- ( kinda like the Soup Nazi on Seinfield) got up in my face and started YELLING that he makes the bisque-personally, I again stated there was no lobster, no lobster flavor, and picked up a spoon of the stuff, he Yelled again, "whats that??" pointing to a piece of orangey red thing- I replied, looks like a carrot, he said "I don't put no carrots in the bisque"- this time he was so close he SPIT on my face!
 Upon tasting that little thing it was a pepper..I did however uncover a 1 cm piece of lobster! He then Yelled "lobster is 24.99 a pound" like I care- my bisque in an egg drop soup take out was 10 bucks! (my husbands place gets FRESH lobster wholesale for much less- hand selected none the less!)
 The waitress tossed my little plastic container in the trash..and I waited for my dining partner to finish her chowder.
 True to their word no more food came our way, as IF I would have wanted to further line his greedy little pockets!
 So now I am left wondering do I need a medical exam for getting some strangers spit in my eye??

First things first. Hands down, the best part about this place is Paul, the owner. A middle aged Italian guy who walks around schmoozing with his clientele, sporting a lobster print shirt/shorts combo, he was very friendly and welcoming. In what was otherwise a very loud and bustling environment, his charm and hospitality made for a comfortable atmosphere. I repeat - lobster print shorts suit. 

As for the food, it was very tasty but some aspects were a bit overpriced. I started with the spicy crab corn chowder, which was good but could've used more crab. The biggest problem was that a bowl of the stuff cost us $8, and a very small cup of another soup my friend got was $5. Definitely not worth it. 

The fried oyster sandwich was solid. The oysters were fried just right and a generous amount was served on a toasted bun. I was also satisfied with the fried zucchini, which they offer as a side with each of their fried seafood sandwiches as a good alternative to their slightly soggy french fries. I tasted some of my friend's crab cake - very tasty with an excellent proportion of crab meat to other ingredients. 

Overall not a bad place to get your fried seafood. It's not cheap, but what seafood restaurant is? Nothing out of this world, but in the end the food really hit the spot.w

Great place! I have been here for several occasions with my friends....including for my birthday. Its a lot of fun and the food is really good! We usually end up eating a lot of it!!!  

This is a very casual dive type of restaurant. No need to get dressed up or anything. It has a real family feeling. My only complaint is that its in obnoxious and tacky Sheepshead Bay. I would love to see this place get relocated to the boardwalk downtown but its been there forever and its a staple. 

The little necks are really good!! :)

Only thing good about this place is the dozen little necks with a bottle of beer.  Dont get anything else, believe me, if your a true Brooklynite, you know where to go for seafood and its not Randazzos

I agree with one of the reviewers, Paul the owner, gives this place ambiance, buster. If you are looking for old-school Brooklyn, look beyond the pseudo-hipster-little cafes that populate nabes like Park Slope. Instead, head to Randazzo's. Oh---and be sure to sample the Mussles di Zuppa, Pasta Mariachi and the "this-must-be-what-heaven-tastes-like" new england clam chowder. The waitresses are lifers from another era---very dedicated to the place. One star off because you will wait a long time to get another drink or your check because it's just that busy and the waitresses tend to not move too fast.

If I lived any closer to this place I'd be here every sunday night.  The restaurant is diner like decor. Bright lights  when you walk in and a feeling of knowing that you are going to get a good deal as you walk through the tables.  

The clam chowder is creamy and flavorful and better than the lobster bisque.  Raw clams and oysters fresh and cheap.  Crab legs were big juicy and oooo soooo goood!  I loved the seafood pasta which is fit to be shared between two people.  Fried zuchini I miss you already.    Their fries were dissappointing, Undercooked...  Soggy.     

CRABLEGS CRABLEGSCRABLEGSCRABLEGSCRABLEGSCRABLEGS  order them!  

Oh! they didn't have steamers on the night I went but I hear those are to die for too!   ill be back to try those very soon.  Enjoy!

Food is barely edible. Crabcakes have a strange seasoning in it that makes it taste odd. Swordfish is passible. Fried calamari is highly recommended. Best thing is that it has things for kids to do while their family eats. Also, It's right by the bay.
This is my favorite local place for pasta and they have there very own home made sauce... mild or spicy so good. The seafood is fresh. Its family owned and the staff is really nice.

Seriously, what is better than a warm summer afternoon spent at an outdoor table with raw clams and beer? The answer is nothing. Especially if you happen to be getting your clams at Rondazzo's. 

The two of us devoured two dozen topnecks on the half shell, a steamed lobster, clam chowder and fried calamari and washed them down with a couple of beers. 

Everything was top notch and aside from clams that I've pulled out of the water myself, these were probably the freshest and most delicious clams I've ever had in my life. That in itself was worth the trip out to Sheepshead Bay. 

All of the other food I had was great, too (though the sauce served with the calamari was a bit too peppery and smokey). Prices are reasonable, the atmosphere is chill and the service is friendly and attentive. 

Rondazzo's also doubles as an Italian restaurant, but I'm not sure I'd ever make it to ordering a pasta dish. With quality raw clams and oysters, steamers, lobster and the like on the menu, I see no reason to order pasta. 

I can extol the virtues of this place for hours, but I'm not going to. You simply should just go experience it for yourself. I guarantee you'll leave fat and smiling...

Amazing fresh, steamed clams.  They were the size of my hands.  This place also had the best New England Clam Chowder I've ever had!!  If I didn't live all the way out in Queens, I'd be at this great seafood restaurant weekly!

Ok so here it goes. I was enjoying my day in sheepshead bay looking at what the locals brought in off the boats. 

I was with the wife and kids and decided why don't we pop in and have some clams and fried shrimp.

I ordered the baked clams and fried shrimp. The waitress was some what disinterested and completely rude. But I still gave her a shot... Why not?  I was with the family. :) 

We'll I love seafood and the baked clams arrived pretty smelly and tasted like pure dirt. I guzzled my beer and said well maybe the shrimps will satisfy. The shrimps came and to my dismay I could of sworn that the guy who owns the place bought a bag of Costco shrimp fried 8 of them and gave them to me as they had no flavor and tasted nothing like the ocean.  You know that no taste feeling you get when u eat those thawed out shrimp which are the fried... No batter either... Is it just me or does anyone else like their shrimp just a tad crunchy???  fooogheetaboutiiittttt huh....

But the cake goes to paying $30 bucks, for ordering something with the abbreviation "mp"  AKA "my price" or market price for  a half pound lobster.... that's right no stuffing no nothing just lobster with drawn butter.. forget about the fries they were so soggy and nasty I wondered if they even heated the oil before attempting to cook them... Man it was badd, terrible bad.

I guess if your bored, want to eat RAW clams and have a cold beer because you CANNOT mess up RAW clams then RENBOZZO's is your place... 

Good LUCK!

Ever since my seafood dining trip to Boston, I've been pining for great seafood. So I eschewed the Dumpling fest and trekked to Randazzo's looking for the fried clams I had recently experienced at No Name. Randazzos came to mind, a place I've passed by numerous times on my way to Manhattan beach but never tried. This place has a rep for good seafood and we were pleased to find the food held up to the rep. The clam chowder was delish, creamy and laden with potatoes wand huge chunks of clams and was nicely spiced.  The fried calamari was crispy and came with a marinara sauce that would have gone great with pasta. I do have to say that the Daily Catch in Boston has spoiled me for calamari anywhere. Even good calamari, like Randazzo's pales. We also had the baked clams; not being a fan of baked clams, I do have to say that under the bread crumb topping, the clams were fresh and definitely didn't need the topping. We didn't try the clams after the waitress told us it was clams strips. She must have been telepathic, because what I wanted were Ipswich clams with tender little bellies. The place had a comfortable, spacious feel and my sister and I lingered over lunch. What is it about these old seafood shacks? The waiters and waitresses seem to have been with them for years. Either the owners are terrific or they get a daily allowance of fresh seafood with their employment. But our lovely gal seemed to have been there for years and she was still so sprightly. Oh, she gets five stars for enthusiasm and service and charm.

Loved the New England clam chowder, the fried calamari, and the mussels in marinara sauce. Mmmmm...delicious. The service was ok but overall would definitely come back. I sat outside, on their benches, and I felt I was at the Jersey Shore. And I mean that in a good way :-). It just felt like a family business, the waitstaff are yelling at each other and it looks like a place where everyone knows your name. Plus, its very laid back. I'm a fan and would love to come back.

I see the appeal of Randazzo's, and the experience is very enjoyable. But the food is not good. Randazzo's has an old "seaside diner" type of vibe: the menu is simple, they only accept cash, and the waitstaff just plops plates of fried seafood on tables (rather than calmly serving dishes). This isn't a place for fancy seafood dishes or courteous service. So I get all that, and I it's a type of place that I could be into.

Except the food isn't good. A restaurant like this only works if the food is good enough to carry the place. The only thing we ate that I truly enjoyed was a hearty plate of steamers. Otherwise, we were all rather disappointed. Oysters required a copious amount of sauce... we couldn't identify the clams in the fried claims... the calamari were serviceable, though they wouldn't have stood out anywhere else.

In the end, I walked out of here having spent more than I would have liked for a meal of this caliber. Our key mistake was not dining outside -- at least that way we would have enjoyed a nice day while we ate less-than-stellar food.

Overall impression: though the atmosphere is definitely classic and the diner feel of Randazzo's lends itself to an enjoyable experience, the food falls far short of expectations, especially considering the fact that this isn't an inexpensive place.

Loved this place! 
Perfect place for a date or just hanging out with friends. My boyfriend and I went for the raw clams... Yum *starts drooling* they were definitely fresh. 
I also had the spicy corn chowder (bad combination in the tummy =x... Don't ask) 

The prices are reasonable. I thought the chowder was too much ($10) but I'm a soup fanatic sooo I caved in. 

The area is beautiful and the Restaurant is family orientated for sure. They also have seating outside nothing fancy, but it's relaxing. Go for it!

I am between 3 and 4 stars with this one but i'm feeling good today :)

I think the place is good, has good seafood and things are fresh (obviously a must :P). My bf unfortunately doesn't eat any seafood so he doesn't enjoy more than the chicken tenders and mozzarella sticks. His parents on the other hand swear by this place. There are a few places that occupy our weekends out with them for "linner" and this is def one of their favs hence the 4th star.

Good place to check out if you've never been :)

The place is very casual but food was very good. Service was also good.
They do accept credit cards and they do have their own parking lot in the back as many of you know parking on Sheepshead Bay could get crazy.
I would not say it cheap, for 4 of us we left around 200 that include beers.
Portions are big so can be shared.

I honestly find this place CRAPPY. The NE clam chowder was okay, and the crab cakes I ordered were...ehh, I've had better from the frozen section at my grocery. Not to mention that our waitress was super rude. I was absolutely disgusted with the service. 

Order a coke and see the size of the bottle they give you. Its the size you'd find in lunchbox of a 1st grader. The waitress dropped the top side of my bun from my crab cake sandwich on the floor and brings back a new one, cold and untoasted. I didnt even eat it like a sandwich. Probably the worst crab cakes I ever ate. 

On a good note a tasted some Cherrystones off of my friends plate and they were good. Then again, they were raw (i think) so how hard could that have been?

Two words: CRAB CAKES.

Randazzo's is a Sheepshead staple.  Much like Gino's in Bensonhurst, Grimaldi's of DUMBO, and Garguilio's of Coney Island, Randazzo's is a rite of passage for any Brooklynite.  If you have never been, I highly recommend a trip to South Brooklyn to check it out.

Go ahead, and tell em I sent yah!
Rude cranky old ladies waiting tables... Food is bland.. Its good for a quickey if you crave seafood in sheepsbay. Other wise i would not recommend...

Randazzos is the last of a era, once sheepshead bay was nothing but a bunch of clam bars and joint's, back in the day those who where in the know would eat at "Joe's" but never in the restaurant, only in the clam bar, you could get cherry stones, as big as your palm, great calamari, and the best new york style chowder I've ever had, but I digress, Randazzos was always about the sauce, it was dark rich, thick, and rumor has it that the sauce pot had been cooking since the day the restaurant started continuously, it was the best sauce in Brooklyn for seafood, 

Now a days I'm less then impressed by Randazzos, I use to be a regular to their clam bar, the best cherry stones in Brooklyn with the exception of the Nathan's clam bar when it was still open, 

The best deal was the cold lobster, it use to be $10 bucks, and was always about a pound and a quarter, 

Their calamari was the best, flash fried after being soaked in milk and lightly breaded and you didn't have to ask for tentacles, ad that biscuit that everyone's complaining about, its suppose to be that way, rock hard slightly softened with sauce, 

Now a days the foods OK., the change in kitchen staff has a lot to do with it I think, back in the day mom's Randazzos would be supervising the kitchen, tasting the sauce, the bisque, etc., the fry cooks where Italian and Portuguese, had been there since the dawn of time, and where rude and crusty, it was all part of the ambiance,

Now a days the cooking staff is largely Hispanic or Mexican i suspect, the food is OK. but its not the same, the sauce has a decidedly south American flare and the last time I had the lobster bisque which i agree was more like chowder then a true bisque, it had so much celery and barely any lobster, and tasted like it had been thickened with flour instead of cream a real disappointment at the price, 

I'll still eat here but now a days I'm more likely to go to Jordan's lobster dock for the calamari then stop here their sauce is almost as good, and the portions twice the size although you have to ask for tentacles and they don't always have them, and for those of you that don't like the biscuit there none with the calamari at Jordan's, just squid and sauce.

and for those of you in wheelchair like my wife the restaurant is handicapped accessible but the clam bar, and the bathrooms are not and there are no handicapped accessible picnic tables.

If your like me, when you see a small gift box, you automatically think "oh great crappy gift" but little did you know that besides you being uber shallow and judging the gift by size , inside  that small gift box was actually THE blue box... 

this leads me to Randazzo's. My family and I have been going to this place for YEARS. Don't judge the outside ( relatively simple, shouts more of a little random place than a restaurant) The food inside caught me by surprise. Delicious. The marinara sauce ( i like it on the side) is to die for. 

This place is such a family place. You have Vinny the owner greeting you at night BY YOUR NAME ( if your there often enough) at certain busy evenings, to Karen ( don't remember  rest of their names, sorry) taking your order.. this place is cutely decorated with a whole by the ocean theme. There are portraits of deceased family members on the wall referencing either a great aunt etc. you really get the family owned sense here and well, like you know THEIR family.

The staff is very nice and you gotta love the Brooklyn accents. On busy evenings there is definitely a lot of activity happening there from the screaming " I NEED THREE CALAMARRRR!"  to the busboy whizzing around collecting your dishes and filling your plastic cups up.

I must admit that the calamari isn't the same anymore.. Its still delicious but its not as crispy as it used to be. My favorite is the salmon. I get this EVERY TIME. Sometimes I like to switch it up, perhaps a linguini fra diavlo with some shellfish. (scungili, mussels, clams etc)

I love the french fries here. Not greasy and perfectly crunchy, but salmon is the way to go. I crave it sometimes when I just HAVE to go all the way to Brooklyn to get my fix. Randazzo's is perhaps one of the VERY few reasons I will trek all the way to Brooklyn. 

I have had almost everything on the menu, you cant really go wrong with anything.

Come here if you can. (especially during the summer)Maybe you will see Vinny.. or maybe me haha.

I know this is a seafood place, but I thought the fries were REALLY good here. One of the more crispy and tasty fries that I've had. I'd come back here just for the fries! 

I also had a cup of lobster bisque which was good and really filled me up. I had to take most of my linguine and lobster sauce to go. Great the next day! 

The service was also great. Very friendly and welcoming. I would definitely come back.

I love this place. It's classic Brooklyn, with waitresses old enough to be your grandma and sassy enough to keep you in line, unpretentious decor and simply amazing food.

I'm a creature of habit. Spicy crab chowder and an order of fried clams with medium sauce on the side. The calamari is also delicious.

The prices have increased significantly since I started coming here. I don't go as frequently, but the food's to delicious to stay away from forever.
This place was really disappointing. The fried calamari was soggy and tasteless. I will not be coming back.

Absolutely love this. Great Oysters, great fries, great main dishes, I've started to come here nearly every week. It's right on the bay, so eat and walk off the fullness. Family run and they just don't hire any shmo.

Can't say enough about this spot.
The best Seafood Fra diavolo I have ever had.  The lose a star because they are overpriced for south Brooklyn.   But really good food if you  have the money!

OK, I like to be fair so I'm amending my earlier, more harsh review.  I'll say this up front....if you stick to the raw bar items, i.e., raw clams and raw oysters, you'll be happy.  As for the menu items I sampled and this was my previous Yelp, I came here on recommendation from a relative.  I walked  out disappointed and considerably poorer.   Fried clam strips  were pretty tasteless and came with nothing, no f. fries, no coleslaw, nothing.  The baked clams were also tasteless, with way too much bread crumbs, the Italian kind from the can that taste like they're from a can.  The whole clam underneath was just a tasteless blob lost in the breading.  The raw clams were fresh and tasty, though next time I would go with the little necks as the cherry stones were too big for my liking.  Not a fan of cream soups, I had the spicy corn chowder since it was pretty nippy sitting outside.   It was passable (not great) with an undertone of sherry and tarragon that was, at least,  not overdone.  I think if I had stuck to the soup and a glass of Pinot I might have been more inclined to give the place two stars.  The Marinara sauce was the best part about Randazzo's but that's just not a big enough draw in my opinion.  Here's my advise to those craving delicious fresh and reasonably priced seafood.  Spend the extra money on gas and take a scenic ride out to the North Fork of Long Island.   Hit either Buoy One in Riverhead (indoor or patio dining) or Braunn Seafood Market in Cutchogue ( take out and outdoor dining).  Randazzo's  might have been good once, but there is just nothing appealing about either Randazzo's Clam Bar or the entire Sheepshead Bay area.

Great day wandering and shopping brownstone Brooklyn. Sun started popping through the clouds on a lazy summer afternoon so decided to take a Brighton boardwalk stroll and hit up Sheepshead Bay. Hadn't been since I was a kid and boy has it changed. Very few of the old Italian American joints remain and sadly beautiful Old Lundy's is long gone but with a damn good Russkie gourmet food market named Cherry Hill in its place. Very happy to see old Randazzo's Clam Bar still standing. Had to check it out. Place was a blast! Bustling, with picnic tables outside, big clam bar where they shuck the little necks and cherrystones right in front of you and set up with a cold brew. Grabbed a table and had a couple dozen baked cherrystones, fried "calima" with hot sauce, linguini with white clam sauce, shrimp oreganato and lobster fra diavolo. Awesome, fun feast and very reasonable. Even the servers were a hoot and very friendly, in a gruff South Brooklyn way. Then hit up the food place at Lundy's for some great ice and gelato which we ate while strolling along the water checking out the fishing boats. Forget the Manhattan faux Italian American wannabes, if you want a taste of Ole Skool Brooklyn Cugine Cuisine, Randazzo's is the place!

Went there for lunch with a couple of friends. Randazzo's is known for good simple seafood. So how do you ruin a good lunch experience?  A waitress with an attitude and overcooked inedible fried calamari.

Having the desire for some seafood, we headed from Queens to Sheepshead Bay with the intention of Randazzzo's, but were keeping our options open. I had not previously eaten at this small, casual eatery, but my mom who took me for fathers day had been prior. The place was quite busy, but we were ushered to a table within minutes, by the busboy, who was wearing many hats this day., it appeared they were short staffed. For starters we ordered the calamari (hot) daily special and the dozen raw little-neck clams. They have a shucker in the restaurant's front portion, that was receiving orders verbally by the waitstaff "One NECK!!" Clams were meaty and fresh, the calamari was not frozen, breaded properly, not stiff nor spongy, so app's got an immediate high rating. Lets not leave out the small details here. The bread that the table gets, was fresh, crusty and plentiful, the water was server to us in a large plastic pitcher, we self poured, saving us and the waitstaff time and effort. Our waitress was about 55+ in age, she must have had 10+ tables, she moved around the joint with ease, knew her business, didn't mince words and was overall a great server. Small Details. I'm a big guy and a was beginning to feel a little full, right on cue, out from the kitchen came the Shrimp Calamari (red sauce in picture), unfortunately the same sauce as the calamari app, which I figured was the case prior to ordering it) and the Shrimp Randazzo.  (white sauce in picture) 7 quality shrimp and 3 clams, over a huge serving of linguine. I'm not sure of the sauce make up of the Randazzo, but it was a white wine, garlic, butter lemon zest flavor. Very light, tangy, but not overpowering. 
Conclusion: Great menu, nice list of specials (ask the prices first) very nice for family, a date, take out, or slurping down a few raw ones at the raw-bar. Budweiser 12oz bottles were $5.00, that was a bit more than is appropriate for this establishment, but with all of the positives, it was easy to overlook.

My parents and I have been coming to this place since 1987.  That in itself is a reason why this place gets 5 stars. 

The reasons we go back are the raw clams on the half shell, the fried calamari, the service and the SAUCE.  The clams are always fresh and plump.  The fried calamari is always cooked right by Emilio.  The sauce is just the right touch of sweet and acidic, plus you got to choose hot or mild.  And the service... Always attentive.  They make you feel at home here.  These are true Brooklyn ladies.

Over the years, I've seen so many changes but nothing that hurt the establishment, the service or the food.  If anything, it made it better.  They added more food like pasta dishes.  They had this gigantic tv to watch the football games on Sundays.  And the parking meters were taken out, not necessarily by Randazzo's, but parking was always free, if available.

We don't come here as much since we moved to the Bronx, but whenever we're nearby, it's our first choice.

After a day at the beach, I was craving some fried seafood.  

This area of Sheepshead Bay has a lot of restaurants and places to shop.  It is nice to go there and eat by the water.

Randazzo's is not a fancy joint... So don't expect to be wowed when you walk in and if you are sitting outside expect to eat out of paper cups (soup) and paper plates.  

However, their mouth watering FRIED SOFT SHELL CRAB SANDWICH was delicious.  Exactly what I needed after a long day in the water.  I order it with Zucchini fries... The fries were not my favorite.

Another thing I liked was their famous Spicy sauce. I had it on the COMBO plate (Scungilli, Mussels, Shrimp, and Calamari.) I believe I licked the plate. 

-----

FYI Despite what people said about the Manhattan Clam Chowder being good... it's not.. It was tasteless.

I took my girlfriend to this establishment for her birthday and was generally happy with the experience. However, we were not prepared for the hours of stomach pain and vomiting that followed. 

As I type this my girlfriend is doubled over the toilet heaving chunks of calamari and I'm nursing the worse stomach pain I've ever experienced, looking to the heavens for answers and cursing Randazzo's name.

Do not go here.

Seafood was fresh, but if you are looking for good service, this is not the place. After ordering, we had to request forks and after we got our food, we had to ask for napkins and waited with our food for them for five minutes. Our waitress didn't even bring them over, I had to get up myself and ask for them from a bus boy. All in all, don't recommend it. Nice location though.

The food is AMAZING! The price is a little too high and the place is sometimes dirty, but moslty clean. The people there are friendly and its not that a crowded place. I went there today with my aunt and granny, with my sister and parents and we all enjoyed a perfect lunch!
Their seafood is so fresh and delicous! Everything is fried, or at least it seems that way to me. I had steamers for the first time there. Yum!
Randazzo's is where I go for my Lobster Bisque fix. I normally get the Bowl along with the Chicken Parm over Pasta. The last time we went, we had the Raw Oysters and they were GREAT.

The battle between truth and sentimentality.

The Sentimental

I've been going here since i was a teenager. Whenever the weather got nice and we needed a break from Flatbush, my mom and I would head to Sheepshead Bay and 9 out of 10 times end up eating at Randazzo's.

I've spent many summer nights here talking about my future plans, worrying over future plans and laughing at past mistakes with my mom here.  
I'm pretty sure my love of oysters, clams and pretty much all things nautical started here. 

So in my heart it's a 5 stars
 
But  the truth is , for someone who doesn't share my sentimental attachment , it's probably not.

The prices have increased and while the food is quite good, it seems too pricey. Most entrees range from $18- $23 and , of course , lobster is market price ($$$). Oysters  average about $2 to $2.50 each. At this price should I be served drinks in plastic cups and be eating with plastic utensils and disposable plates ?  The service is casual here, almost too casual. You may have to track down a waitress to get drinks, etc.  While the service was fine when it was consider cheap eats or casual food I think the price increases lead you expect more.

Again I have no qualms with the food, as I write this I want to go and get their Shrimp Fra Diavolo. It's Shrimp, mussels and clams over linguine in a delicious, spicy tomato based sauce. Sauce so wonderful you want to sop up the remainder with your bread. 

But the waitress never brought you bread........... 

I'll still go, especially when mom comes to town, but truth be told it's
 A-OK.

I grew up in Brooklyn and spent the last 25 years filling my belly with mussels and red sauce. I was there this past week with my mom and wife and it was just the best. I had the mussels marinara - awesome. My wife had chicken parm - a huge portion, tender juicy, crispy with a ton of pasta. My mom, bless her heart ordered the soft shell grabs and did not ask the price. They were 40 bucks. I asked her why she did not ask what the price of the food cost (the menu says seasonal), she said she is always being taken out by guys and never had to pay a bill for soft shell crabs. Too funny.

You can't go wrong at this place. The wait staff is getting younger, they used to be all very old women, like your grand mother taking care of you, and they still rock. Ours was a young hottie. 

Go to randazzos and fill your soul

The Worst ! Don't go.  I was mislead by Yelp!   They should do a kitchen nightmares on this place.  

I asked if the lobster was fresh and the waitress said yes, although she also said she didn't like it and wouldn't recommend it, but i thought "how bad can fresh lobster be?" take a live lobster and boil it...
I got my lobster less than 10 min later, and it was only warm, cut in half, and the claws were cracked...suspect.. 
I tried a piece of tail meat first...so rubbery i couldn't swallow it (no exaggeration).  foolishly, i tried a piece of the claw, after gnawing on that piece of rubber i actually swallowed it.  that was enough, at 28 bucks for a slightly better than one pound lobster i decided to talk to the manager.

Long Story slightly abbreviated...
the manager finally admitted to cooking the lobster in the morning, and keeping the cooked lobster on ice, and reheating per order, but wouldn't admit that that's not fresh...i didn't have to pay for it (small plus), but still a sad sad waste of fresh lobsters...

based on my argument with the manager/ "head chef", and his outlook on fresh food, i would never eat anything from this place. 

I apologize to all the sentimentals... this happens so often with multi-generational restaurants, go in and say hello, but eat somewhere else.
i love to get a dozen raw clams and drink a nice cold corona here on a nice day.
Food seemed good. Until I came home and felt nauseous the whole night. No one else at the table for 30 got sick so I suspect it was the only thing unique that I ate: solf-shell crab on a bun.

A staple of great Italian seafood specials.

I great up in Sheepshead Bay and to this day still try to get to Randazzos on warm summer nights.  The red sauce is some of the best I ever had.  No frills food w/ lots of flavor.  Try the Lobster Fradiavalla, which is enough for 2 ppl.
Little neck AND Cherrystones! Any way you want them. Thank goodness real clam bars still exist.
Very casual dining but the food is consistently delicious. I've been going here for years and have never found fault with the service.

The BEST lobster fradiavlo bar none! Every year for the past 25 years I ask my mother where she wants to go for Mother's Day, her birthday, or any other occassion I get to take my mom on, and her reply is always the same "I am in the mood for Randazzo's". I tried taking her to other places, nicer in decor or better known, or fancier  (this place is very, very casual)  but when I tell you the food at Randazzo's is always better and I always hear it afterward, "we should of just gone to Randazzo's, Ok mom!! . The baked clams are done perfectly. when I go somewhere else and I order the baked clams, I always compare them to Randazzo's. and the Manhattan clam chowder,is just the best.  The prices have def gone up and its a bit too pricey for its location and the kind of restuarant it really is.  But since I only go there a few times a year with my mom, I just say the hell with it. 

I remember when it was a hole in the wall many, many years ago and the food was amazing since then just not as expensive, but really good food!

Was at Randazzo's 3 months ago and still can't stop thinking about it. There's a certain old world Brooklyn charm, but you're definitely not going for the decor. It's all about the seafood and everything I tasted among 5 orders was delicious, from cooked to raw, and the famous red sauce is as good they claim. Place was packed, but the owner still found a chance to come by and crack a few jokes. If you want fancy, go to Manhattan. This may be the best food I've ever eaten in Brooklyn.

Randazzo's has been a staple of Brooklyn for decades. I love that the seafood here is always fresh and the staff are all family. My personal favorite dish is the soft shell crab sandwich (when it's in season) and in addition I like to order the spaghetti with the great tomato sauce. The calamari and new england clam chowder are pretty good as well. If you're in the neighborhood, check this joint out.

Randazzo's is definately my go to place for an authentic NYC clam bar. Definately casual dining for sure, but they hold the patent on the best hot calamari sauce in the world! I'll wait for a seat at the counter. I like the calamari steamed with hot sauce. A little less decadent than the fried version. My wife always has the lobster bisque and a side of spagetti with the hot sauce. I think all three are world class. The steamers are by far the best available on the planet and if you like spicy, try the spicy crab bisque.
I'll certainly concede that I like my food spicy, but Randazzo's has truly mastered the art of making spicy seafood delicious as well.

Emmons Ave is full of great restaurants and finally one night we decided to go to Randazzo's Clam Bar for seafood.

We had:

1. Clam Chowder - Delicious! It's how clam chowder should be made, thick consistency and full of ingredients. 
2. Crab Cakes with Fries - Again, delicious!
