3. Fried Scallops with Fries - Just delicious!
4. Fresh Oysters - Wow, so fresh and just delicious!
Oysters, scallops, calamari, OH MY! Actually, all caps not needed. It was good though. Brooklyn Lager, too.
I dont get the hype about this place. Its a bit dingy and low class. Prices are hight and I've had better sea food. Services is plain old bad.

Late night stop for fired clams and calamari. This family owned business has great fried seafood starters. Careful with that spicy marinara that stuff is potent. I will return to try the lobster! and the other surf dishes!

Not the cheapest place out there but the QUALITY is top notch.  You get what you pay for here.  Randazzo's never upsets.

1 Issue in this day and age why the kiddie cups and micro sized soda bottles.  Makes me feel like I am on an airplane

Soups are good oysters/clams are good the calamari as well. This place is expensive though and the main courses are not that good. If you dont mind spending the extra bucks for a few good appetizers go for it.

I had late dinner with the kids and friends here a couple of weeks ago...

The fish is very fresh!

That is about it though...
This is a family friendy place serving comfort seafood-italian.
The prices were a little high for what the restaurant had to offer.

We had, calamari, squid, sole, shrimps, chicken parm....everything was fresh but the quality of the food is average.

Would go back with kids because its very accomodating.....

Ordered the Fish fry platter, Zuppa di Mussels in white sause, and Lobster bisque.  This place was great.  The people and service.  Normally, I heard that this place usually has a line out of the door, but today we were lucky.  Everything was awesome except for the price.  I checked another seafood place in Staten Island and the prices were cut in half.  Since living in the NYC area, I can expect high prices for seafood, only because seafood must be imported due to the Hudson River not having viable seafood that is eatable.  If both these restaurants have to import their seafood and one is way higher than the other, I tend to suspect the other is way overpriced.  Other than that and the fact that this place can't or doesn't make their own tarter sauce, I have to deduct a half star.

One of my favorite seafood places in brookyn

If you want some amzing seafood this is the place. PRices are not low but well worth it...

Def try the Alaskan king crab legs they are amaing
and there oysters

But last but not least there amzing hot sauce.//

I've been coming here since I was a kid, like my father before me (Jedi style) and it remains great. Prices have increased over the years, but that's to be expected. I still love getting steamers, white clam chowder, calamari, and shrimp scampi. If you want seafood on this side of Brooklyn, just go here. Casual and delicious.

Food was excellent. The fried calamari is the best with lemon and marinara sauce. There lobster is cook very well, there service was excellent as well. I have no complaints about this place. You pay for what you get and thats excellent food, so its going to be on the pricey side. There food and seafood is always fresh, what do you expect your dining right by the water. I had no regrets. Since i was treating that day hey my bill was less than $120. Not bad for 2 lobster meals, some starters and drinks. Than after that you can just walk around by the water. Best thing ever.
Not only is everything good foodwise,the waitresses are the nicest people ever.They remind me of my Italian aunts growing up

the best calamari i've ever had in 40 years. i recommend this place to all of my friends and they thank me for it. this place is a real deal CLAM BAR. do not expect an extremely fancy restaurant or that type. its basic and old school. they serve amazing seafood and thats all.

Food was decent but nothing great. It was definitely not worth the prices they charge, especially since there is nothing upscale about the restaurant itself. From the decor to the tiny coke bottles and plastic cups we had to use, the whole experience didn't warrant the $55+ bill charged for me and my boyfriend (we didn't even order anything special, just oyster sandwiches and soup).

Their soups and chowders are the best. I love the spicy crab chowder and manhattan clam. 

Their calamari is delish especially with their spicy marinara sauce. Their pasta dishes are ok and they are a bit on the pricey side. The one thing that does annoy me is that the soda they serve is in those little 6 or 8 oz glass bottles and they charge like $2.00 for it. Why not cans? 

One time I had the raw oysters and got very sick. I would still come back but prob won't order their raw food anymore.

What I mainly come here for, are the steamers & Clams! It is divine. The atmosphere makes me feel like i took a trip to Maine. The Lobster Bisque was a tad off, it isn't what you'll eat at higher end. It's more homemade style. So if your feening for the soup. Just a heads up! As for the Chicken Parm. Nothing of special in any sorts. It was tender and juicy. The marinara has it's own tart flavor. Not too overwhelming. Portion is perfectly fit if your not on beast mode! So if your not feeling for a road trip & just craving for some fresh seafood. Stop on by the Bay, off Brooklyn.

Great Soft shell crab sandwich + zucchini fries and very fresh Oysters, Cherry Stones and Little Necks!!!  And the crab cakes are absolutely the best of anywhere I've ever tried (and I have tried many crab cakes)!   Very meaty.
huge portions!!! lots and lots of mussels!! yum!!! food was great, decor wasnt too fancy but again it's the food that sells the place!! definitely going back!!!
Nice atmosphere, right on the other side ofthe sheepshead bay. Good food, crab cakes had huge lumps of crab. Waitress screaming across the place the whole time, but hey, its Brooklyn,  gotta love it.
City island has nothing on this one restaurant, homey, good food & good prices! Seafood is always fresh. If you want good food you have to come here!

My friends and I went fishing from the Sheepshead Bay pier and was starving when we got back.  Randazzo's looked very promising from the outside and we were just too hungry to hunt around for a place to eat.  Boy do I wish we had just sucked it up and found another place to spend our money.
First of all, Randazzo's looks a bit like a diner so we did not expect such high Manhattan priced entrees.  I don't mind paying money for good food, but the food here is just okay.  We ordered the calamari as a starter and the calamari was pretty good, but the bread that came with it was hard as a hard.  I seriously thought I was going to chip a tooth biting into the thing.  For my entree I had the fried fish plate which again was just okay for me at $28.  
I would have given this place 3 stars, but had to deduct one for the poor service we got there.  We were sitting in the back and tried many times to get the attention of the many waitresses standing literally behind us just chit chatting, but none of them even gave us a second glance.  We had to wait at least 5 minutes to get our bill and then forever for them to acknowledge that we were ready with our credit cards.  We finally ended up just paying at the counter ourselves since none of the waitresses seem to give a damn.  I would definitely never go there again when there are so many other better restaurants with staff who care about customer service.

My friends called and said we're going to a seafood place in Sheepshead Bay.  I was thinking, "I don't know, it's going to be far and expensive."  I'm so glad I decided to go.

The place looks like a diner... a plain old diner, something I rarely see anymore, so I liked it.  We waited a few minutes for them to clear up a table for our party of 5.  

Like everyone else, I wish the soda came in bigger portions, as I usually need a liter to get through a dinner.

The food was very good, well, everything I tried.  We were sharing everything and I tried just about everything that was ordered.

We ordered:
Appetizers
- fried calamari
- 6 oysters (raw)
- 10 baked clams
- lobster bisque - so-so IMO
- a bowl of mussels 
Entrees
- stuffed fish
- Lobster Randazzo (comes with pasta)
- Linguine with lobster in red sauce - so-so IMO
- Shrimp Randazzo (comes with pasta)

Aside from the two IMO so-so dishes, I liked everything else.  

The service was very good.  The waitress came by at least 6 times solely to make sure everything was to our liking.  

Last but not least, I got to wear the lobster bib !

This is the spot for seafood.
Plain interior, nothing fancy.
But OMG- the food is unbelievable.
I've been coming here for at least 20 years, and will for many more....
Everything is amazing, but their #1 item is their fried calamari and sauce.... 
Cooked fresh (as it should be), lightly floured, and the SAUCE is ridiculous. 

Recommend the following (this is what I get every time !):
start with a bowl of New England Clam Chowder- nobody does it better....
then, go for a dozen or 2 of Little Neck Clams (their horseradish is bangin)...
finish off with fried calamari with medium or hot sauce (i go hot)....

Trust me....
Can't be beat....

I guarantee it!

Randazzo's is probably my favorite seafood restaurant. Partly because I grew up going there but mostly because of the excellent fresh seafood and the great people who work there. It's an old school, not fancy, very laid back place. If you are going there for the first time and your party is 2-3 people, I'd recommend sitting at the counter where the service is always fast and friendly.Their soups are great starters, so are the raw clams and oysters if you're into that. You really can't go wrong with anything you order there now that I think about it. Fried calamari, zuppa di mussels, stuffed shrimp, seafood randazzo, crab cakes, scungili, are some of my favorites. Ask for hot (sauce) on the side and your good to go. I will point out though that Randazzo's is probably more of $$$ than a $$. Good seafood ain't cheap.

I like coming here in the summer as I feel that seafood is more in season. I've never been here for a full meal but have been here so many times just for calamari and mussels. I love love love their mussels, I think it's the sauce they make, which is perfect to dip the bread into too.

I have been a patron of Randazzo's since the mid 1970's and make it a point to come here at least once a month. My spot is at the counter where I am served professionally by Armando and Emilio. The menu is very simple but perfect. Believe it or not, my favorite meal other than the seafood is the side order of spaghetti with the famous medium sauce. Another amazing feature about Randazzo's is when you walk in the front the door, the aroma overwhelms and prepares you for an amazing meal. I can only click on 5 stars, but I give them 10 stars.

We had a great meal at Randazzo's.  We all asked for water and the waitress brought us a large pitcher.  Orders of fried zucchini with sauce kept coming out of the kitchen to many of the patrons.  We ordered that, along with the fried scallop platter,  soft-shell crab platter, and shrimp platter.  Everything was excellent.  The sauce (and I am not a big red sauce eater)  was amazing.  They have the best medium sauce I have ever tasted.   The same with the fried zucchini and french fries,  I don't usually rave over french fries, but they were excellent.   We will definitely go back again, and try some other things like the raw bar, and clam chowder.
Best ever. This place makes me want to move back to Brooklyn. Beautiful seafood, fresh, amazing sauce.

The food isn't up to the reputation.  On the $22 combination plate, I could tell the difference between the scungilli (conch), mussels, shrimp, and calamari (squid), but nothing was really fresh or sweet.  Also the hot sauce was just barely hot.

For a Saturday lunch on a cool but not uncomfortable day, the place was nearly empty.

Everything was clean, and service was good, though not particularly attentive.

I was bored and won't be back.

Not bad at all.   The seafood is very FRESH and the service was alright.  For a weekday, it was pretty packed.  You can also notice a lot of locals who frequent this area.  Basically, if you are allergic to seafood, best not to go to get tempted :)
It is a laid-back joint that looks like it can be debuted on DDD.  

The shrimp was very fresh and also had the calamari.  I was not with enough people to order more..but looking at everybody else's dish, I noticed the filet of sole was FRESH and yummy... it flakes right into the fork.  Too bad it wasn't me who was eating it, haha.  Then I noticed another lobster dish - it also looked very juicy and nice.  

Will come here with more people next time so I can try more dishes.  Then that way, I can give a more thorough review.

This place has the best seafood. Got here on a weeknight, and the place was packed.
Sat down and order my favorite dozen of clams, oysters, and then a share pasta dish with my girls. 

The best place for quick seafood. The service was tremendously great, and friendly waitresses. The food is fantastic and quick.

One of my favorites for seafood. Be prepare to wait for a table. Worth it..!!

I took my brother here to celebrate his birthday at this no BS & no frills seafood restaurant. Almost everything but the plates the food came out on was disposable and our waitress was fast and to the point but friendly and made us feel welcome. We ordered a sample of almost everything on the menu from raw to cooked and baked to fried seafood to chowder, pasta and soup. I mostly stuck to the cooked seafood because I was going on a road trip the next day and didn't want to risk stopping to take a dump every 30 minutes but the others in my party said the raw portions were just as good as the cooked and they didn't even get sick afterwards.The prices were pretty fair for the quality of the food they served. The only downside was the almost hour long wait but being able to watch the sun go down and an abnormally huge moon come up by the bay made it a little more bearable on an unseasonably cold spring night.

Very nice staff members. All the food we ate had a fresh taste. It's not a fancy place but you get great service and a delicious meal.
I was here for lunch so it wasn't crowded and we were seated promptly.

There are many good reasons why Randazzo's has been a Brooklyn staple for nearly a hundred years. It is because of delicious food, friendly service, and a cozy atmosphere. I should note that I have not had a chance to go here for a while, but it lived up to my fond memories of eating here. Immediately, Joey, Pauly's son, who was very welcoming like his father and mother Jackie (RIP) greeted my mom, her friend, and myself and seated us at a comfortable, large round table in the rear. As I was walking in, Emilio, one of the fry cooks who I remember, greeted me as if I were an old friend after he recognized me. After being seated, a very friendly young waitress came by and took our orders. I ordered one of my favorites, an order of Plain Fried Shrimp with Medium Sauce and Fries while my mom's friend ordered Fried Shrimp with Fried Zuchinni. My mom, who has many food allergies and keeps kosher somewhat, brought her own food and just ordered a Perrier. Fifteen minutes later, my food and my mom's friend's food arrived and we tucked in. The Plain Fried Shrimp, which are basically fried shrimp without the breading, were sweet, crisp, a nice large size, and definitely fresh. The fries were crisp and filled to the brim with potatoey goodness. The Medium sauce that accompanied the shrimp was tomatoey with a nice kick. My mom's friend also very much enjoyed his Fried Shrimp which were plump and he found pleasantly sweet as well. The waitress, who was a young girl, was attentive without being obtrusive and brought out our food and took our plates back in a timely fashion.As we ate, we basked in the atmosphere, which while nothing fancy, was down to earth and clean with wood paneling on the walls and nautical Knicks and other memorolbilia around. While our meals along with an iced tea, Perrier, and Diet Coke were not cheap at about $47.50, it was still a good value considering the quality and portion size. Like one of the signs by the fryer states, "Cheap seafood isn't fresh and fresh seafood isn't cheap," which holds true somewhat as good seafood is not always cheap. All in all, Randazzo's is a great stop for seafood if you are in Brooklyn!

Sick and they don't care.  My wife got VERY sick from their Little Neck clams.  Nausea, diarrhea, vomiting. (See the link: http://safeoysters.org/consumers/index.htm )

I don't see this as a big issue. It happens.  The problems is Randazzo's was obnoxious, arrogant and refused to believe anyone could EVER get sick from their seafood.  Review: Food is great.  People are not.

UPDATE:  The NYC health department emailed me for me to give me their phone number after they read my review.  Guess what...this is NOT the first complaint they've had.  They have had several incidences of serious illness from this place.
NASTY-- if leaving zero stars would be possible I would... everything we ordered was what they call "Seafood" disgusting flavorless pre-frozen and soggy--their food literally made me sick=-EW!

This place is an awesome, seaside, open-layout restaurant. Casual, exquisitely fresh out-of-the-ocean seafood for a fair price. 

From the Raw Bar, we got the cherry clams and the oysters. Yum. Fresh. Ocean. The clams were huge! It was actually rather hard for me to swallow. 

Then we got the Manhattan Clam Chower and the Lobster Bisque. The Manhattan Clam Chowder was filled with seafood and you can actually taste the scallops and the clams in it. The lobster bisque was rich and more like a classic clam chowder but with large chunks of lobster in it. I personally thought that the chowder really overpowered the taste of the lobster. You actually couldn't really tell there was lobster until you actually looked!

Wanted to get the fried zucchnini because I was in the zucchini kind of mood. They are addicting! And the cocktail sauce is just the best. They have something in it that gives is a certain "umph."

We then got the pink pasta layered with seafood. The Marchieta (sp?). The pink sauce was less sauce and more about emphasizing the flavor of the calamari, shrimp, and clams. Basically it was a bunch of fresh seafood layered on top of a lot of noodles, sitting in a "pink sauce." This is not your classic Italian pink sauce. 

I saw the stuffed lobster on the table next to us and it looked absolutely mouthwatering. I am getting that next time, as well as the caimari.

This is the worst restaurant I have ever been to. I have never been to a restaurant where the waiters are so obnoxious and rude, and the food didn't have any flavor at all. Upon arriving I asked for a table for 5 and the hostess gave us a number, soon after another party of 5 came in and he offered them a table outside instead of asking me, who came in first. When we finally  got a table outside the table was dirty and the waitress didn't come by until 10-15 minutes later. She didn't even greet us! She just asked us what we wanted and basically rushed us with our orders. There were other waiters/busboys that were there which we basically had to call over every time we wanted something because no one ever came by to check up on how we were doing with the service/food. Inclusively, I asked for a glass of water, the guy came by and seemed like he was bothered by the request walked away without answering yes or no, and I never got my glass of water. I LOVE the fact that they have a sign inside over the register that reads "CHEAP SEAFOOD IS NOT FRESH, FRESH SEAFOOD IS NOT CHEAP." And let me tell you that at that point, I would much rather have had cheap seafood, because I'm pretty sure it would have made up for the TASTELESS,  BLAND, STALE, and NOT FRESH, fried fish we had. The best part is that it came between the cheapest of the cheapest burger bread anyone can find, the type you would find in school lunchroom. Who knows how old that fish was, and that damn thing cost almost $20 - so much for FRESH expensive food. I wish it was fresh and tasty, I would of gladly enjoyed my $20 fried fish. Oh yeah, and for that price, you would at least expect the restaurant to make their own tartar sauce! I will NOT be going back to this place. Horrible, just horrible.

Likes: 

Everything is fresh 

The fact that some of the employees have the phrase, "Can you say galamah?" adorned to the back of their shirts is just as hysterical as some of the characters who frequent here and make you feel as if you are in a scene from Goodfellas or The Sopranoes. 

The crab cakes with a side of the Randazzo's special sauce is enough to get me excited of course ordered along with the fried zucchini sticks. Yum! 

When I ate here with my mom recently, she told me that my father proposed to her in front of Randazzos! 

Dislikes:
-- small plastic cups for water.... some of that sauce is spicy! 
-- it gets really crowded... so you may have to wait to get a table as well as be close to people when you are eating.

Get ready for some good eating at this place
I had the mussel soup with a beer, now thats living.
Classic Brooklyn Italian cooking.

I do agree with the others that the plastic cups look cheesy and service feels a little rushed.
The bill can get a bit pricey depending on the size of your group and what you order. But its fresh seafood so you get what you pay for.

This place was recommended by a friend, and it's in my home area. So, my boyfriend and I decide to try it on Friday night after work. Oh man, my friend was so right, the cherry stone raw clams were so so good. We also try the oyster but it was just alright. My boyfriend & I already said next time we'll eat more cherry stone raw clams and also we want to try the pasta, and the mussels with red or white sauce. anybody who's interest in trying this place?  I sure recommend this place to every human being on earth!!!!!!
The food was good, tasted good. Calamari was great!  the lobster should be less expenssive as it was. I know its a market price but they could work better with that!!! deff going back!

There are establishments that have historically overstayed their welcome and Randazzo's Clam Bar is one of them. The restaurant needs to be retired as the food was appallingly bad. The fried clams were horribly over breaded (you would be better off with frozen clams from the supermarket) and tasteless. The French fried were drowning in grease. I'm off to take a Pepto Bismol.

We were driving through Brooklyn and decided to walk around Brighton Beach. We had never been there before. We thought about Russian food, but kept thinking, "calamari, calamari."
We were so close to Randazzo's...
It was a hot day, so we ordered a couple of beers. Hubby ordered some chowder, Manhattan of course. It was good and hearty.
Then we shared an order of calamari. We ordered the hot sauce on the side. Yummy. The calamari was fresh and had a light crunchy flour dusting.. The sauce was so good I wanted to lick the bowl. 
I cannot speak for the other food. I have only ordered calamari here.
You don't come here for decor. Yes, the plastic cups are a bit tacky, but who cares?
We came here on a Tuesday afternoon, around 2 and it was not crowded.
The service was fast and friendly.
I look forward to returning!

The food here is amazing. Their sauce is to die for. My family and I went here a week ago and we were practically scraping the sauce off our plates. The pasta is made just right and the raw bar is as fresh a can be. Some of the servers weren't super friendly, but the food made up for it. One pf their servers did let me use their wi-fi though.
       This is definitely a place I would recommend to friends and anyone who enjoys fresh seafood. I've never had an upset stomach after eatting their raw clams and oysters, unlike a few other places that served the same. If you enjoy clam chowders, their Manhattan and New England is delicious. Five stars all the way.

it's italian seafood. they specialize in italian food with seafood as their main ingredients. dined here during our visit in NY upon the recommendation of my BF's father.  the neighborhood is very nice with a view of the river across the street.  most of the restaurants on this street look fancy with outdoor seating, but this one is slightly different. there is no outdoor seating and the main dining area looks more like a get in/get out type of joint. definitely nothing fancy about it. 

the price on the other hand says another story. my plate, the Shrimp Randazzo, was just slightly under $20 (cant remember the exact amount), and the BF had something that was Market Value in red sauce. but my plate was so big, i was only able to eat half of it.  eating here made me felt like i was preparing to fend off vampires later because they put so much garlic in the dishes.  it was so much to the point that i had to start fishing them out of my plate. i like garlic, don't get me wrong, but it was just a little excessive for me. 

my order was recommended by the nice old lady who served us and i'm glad she did because i think i was going to order something else and she said i might not like it. they give you water in plastic jugs and cups (fancy, huh?) and you have as much italian bread as you'd like. i'm not a big fan of it but the BF's dad couldn't get enough of it. 

our total bill for the 3 of us was close to $80, and the food was worth the price.

My favorite thing about Randazzo's is that funeral posters, cards, and announcements make up a good deal of the decor. This befits an institution. There's also this, hanging on the wall: http://bit.ly/PZfEEV. 

There's also the food, which is as good as you'd expect it to be given the formica and plastic cups. Yes, the hot sauce is kind of oily. Yes, the bread fell off the Sysco truck three weeks ago. 

But yes, the scungilli is fresh. No, the calamari and fried clams aren't too heavily breaded. And yes, the shrimp are big and good. 

It should be obvious that you're sailing far out to sea if you start ordering pastas and meats.

Decent enough restaurant. I came primarily for the raw clams and definitely loved the cherry stone clams because there was so much meat.  My boyfriend wasn't too happy with them -- said they were salty and that I probably drenched my clams in cocktail sauce and lemon which is why I didn't notice.  

As far as their other food, the shrimp spaghetti was good.  Their "medium sauce" for their cooked combo was delicious.  Mussels were TINY.  The cooked mussel meat was probably a fourth of the size of the raw cherry stone clams... but it was okay.  Scungilli was included in the combo and I wanted to try it for the sake of something new... I wasn't smart enough to look it up first... Not that I wouldn't like sea snail but I was unprepared and once I learned what it was, I got nauseous and refused to touch it. Not the fault of the restaurant. Just a comment.

Like other people said, the small plastic cups were weird, but they gave us a pitcher of water so it wasn't a big deal.

I thought it was funny that the waitresses were all women older than the norm in "hipper" restaurants.   Unfortunately, they weren't all cheer and smiles, but it was getting late, so I won't judge too much.  

Oh, and speaking of lateness, I think it says something that we arrived later than normal dining hours and there was still a good amount of people still eating and people that arrived after us.

Wish I could speak for more of the menu, because everything looked great, but we were in a hurry and I was just in the mood for some steamers. They were big and plump and very flavorful. 

Wait staff was very nice and very helpful.

Loved it and will come back if I'm in the neighborhood.

When I was in NY recently, I stumbled on this restaurant simply  because I was hungry and needed something to eat before I went on a boat ride. By all means there is nothing fancy about this place, decor is bland and boring. The neighborhood is nice though. The menu items seem overpriced. I just ordered the Spicy Crab Corn Chowder and I must say, it was very good. I ate and my soup, paid my bill and I was on my way.

Great food!!! I've been going to Randazzo's since the early 1990s and this is the most consistent restaurant in New York City. I love eating a dozen raw clams (cherry stones) in the summer at Randazzo's. They have great fried calamari and excellent chicken parmigiana. The only reason why I didn't give it 5 stars was because of the lack of ambiance.

Came here on a Friday night around 9pm, although the place was not crowded it was lively. The waitress is such a doll and friendly. We ordered an appetizer, pasta entree and house wines.

The house wines were so adorable. They came in small bottles which were perfect for 2 glasses and only cost $5. The Combo appetizer which includes scungilli (a sort of shellfish), calamari, shrimp, and mussels in mild marinara sauce was amazing. Scungilli and mussels were blanched while the calamari and shrimp was lightly fried to perfection. As for entree, my boyfriend and I shared the Shrimp Randazzo over Linguine. The dish consist of shrimp, clams and mussels in a butter, garlic, lemon and wine sauce. This pasta dish was done really well, I couldn't help but use the bread and dip it into the sauce to soak it all up.

Definitely not a bad place for seafood or some Italian cooking in Brooklyn.
Food is good price is insane for eating bait. Sauce is ok but Vincent's is better.

This restaurant is an oxymoron. Being a seafood place, it consistently overcooks shrimp/mussels/clams. When confronted, the owner angrily replied, "I think we know how to cook seafood" Apparently they don't. The shrimp in Fra Diavalo was the texture of rubber. The sauce, btw, was excellent but the pasta, as soft as the shrimp should have been. It always amazes me that somehow through the generations Italian American chefs have lost the concept of al dente. 
The new England clam chowder is very good, creamy and fatty with a fair amount of clams. But the best dish is a platter of raw littleneck clams, as perfectly uncooked as they should be.
Fantastic dinner, and the staff is incredible. Those people kept those tables moving. Be sure to try the Shrimp Randazzo.

Went here for lunch. The service was good so that's why I will give place 2 stars. We shared a Calamari app which was okay, the sauce was interesting. Besides that the food wasn't good! I got the linguine pasta with mix seafood. The fish (clams, muscles and whatever else)was okay but the sauce or whatever they call it was not. I didn't eat the pasta since it was drenched in that stuff and just ate the fish that was on top. Both, me and my friend didn't feel good after, and I'm assuming it was from that. Will not be coming back.
If you.are looking for real sea food that is not overpriced and tastes great then go to this place. I have gone there many time over the years.

Love this place ! There seafood is very fresh! Their clam chowder is fricken delicious must try it when you to there. The Raw clams and oysters are so fresh and yummy ! Oh and their fried calamari is bomb ! If you're looking for fresh and not pricey seafood spot this is the place to go.

Casual dining on Emmons Ave, both indoor and outdoor seating is available.  They offer delicious, fresh, tasty, filling seafood; and the pasta sauces are amazing. (Yummy!) The crab legs are huge and sooo good definitely worth the arm exercise, to get the meat out, lol. If your in the area make sure you stop by you won't be disappointed. 

Fair prices and a great staff. I am a repeat seafood offender!

Every now and again I come across a restaurant that people rave about and I hear all these amazing things and see people dine there again and again and I read the fantastic reviews and get all excited and go myself to find that it's complete crap!!! And yes, Randazzos is one of them! I am so frazzled, that millions and millions of people claim how delicious it is and they have the best seafood and it's a great place. How? How, how, how?!!! Please tell me!

Me and the bf were in the mood for seafood and we decided on going to Randazzos. All my years of living in Brooklyn, I have never been there, the bfs mother had warned us that it wasn't good and we should have listened! But noooo, everyone says it's great! The reviews are awesome! Blah! First of all the restaurant is not what it seemed. I thought the dining atmosphere would have been wayyy different but it looked like a soup kitchen, whatever. 

Number 1, their prices are outrageous. Super expensive for absolutely nooo reason. We decided on a bowl of clam chowder, a bowl of lobster bisque and an appetizer dish that came with fried shrimp, calamari, mussels and conch with their "house special" marinara sauce that you can get hot or mild. We opted for mild.

10 minutes for two bowls of soup! Clam chowder was whatever, I had better but compared to the lobster bisque it was outstanding. That lobster bisque had some weird flavor going on in it. We then waited at least 30 minutes for that damn appetizer plate, my god! The chef was too busy messing around to fry up some calamari and shrimp! Finally when it came, it was the smallest little dish! This was obviously an appetizer for one! A $22.00 dollar appetizer for one! Not to mention that there were about 2 shrimp, all calamari, and a hard piece of bread right in the middle of the dish so it can be a filler. It was all drowned in the sauce. Completely covered, poured right on top. And I don't know if the "special sauce" was burnt or it was just the flavor but it was not good.

The worst had to be the conch! Boiled, flavorless, and like rubber. Horrible! I've had fresh conch in the Bahamas and it was delicious. This definitely turned me off. If it weren't for the sauce, besides the burnt flavor, I wouldn't have ate it.

Sooo please tell me, I want to understand people, what's so good about this place? I wish I can't point at every person who raves about Randazzos and say "Fail!" And they melt like the wicked witch in the wizard of oz! 

Worst dining experience yet! The ONLY reason I gave them two stars is because of the cute little older Italian waitresses that reminded me of my grandmother. 

That is all!

Worst place ever !!! What a story to tell. I asked the waitress about 2 meal descriptions and ordered a certain meal when my food came it was the second meal that I did not order I told the waitress she brought me a plate I did not want so she said she would switch it not a problem next thing I know a drunk manager came over to our table starting a debate telling me I have to keep that meal cause I ordered it. I felt so embarrassed I asked the waitress to wrap all the meals up to go. I never been to a restaurant in my life that serves you what they want you to eat everyone in the place was staring at us like we were peasants mind you we ordered 2 appetizers before our entree. it was not like we trying to get out of paying I just wanted my correct order. 10oz soda cost $2 no good. I use to eat here a lot as a child guess they are strapped for cash because things change I will never recommend this place to anyone not even my enemies. The funny thing is when we were leaving my fiancé over heard the manager tell the waitress it was her fault- so why would'nt he exchange my meal ? Is this company seriously doing that bad ?Randazzils 2 thumbs down find a different place were the manager isn't piss drunk off wine and actually cares about the reputation of the restaurant & doesn't treat there customers like crap.

This is my first review on yelp. After tonight though I had to write a review.So where do I begin. On this mothers day I went with a small group to eat at this establishment. I had the most unbelievable experience I have ever had while dinning out ( not in a good way).I had heard about this place through a friend. He told me that  not only is the seafood freshly cooked  and delightful but that the atmosphere was something worth witnessing.Well upon arriving to the restaurant the sun was still out and there was a nice breeze off the water so we decided to sit outside. It took about all of 5 minuets before we regretted that decision. Let me state  clearly that the food was as advertised delightful. The calamari with hot sauce the table had was very enjoyable. There was one issue and the main reason I will never go back to this restaurant. The issue with my dinning experience was the service. I had a waiter which was a bit of a shocker because my friend who recommended the restaurant said the woman waitresses make the atmosphere.  This Jersey shore wannabee ( I would of preferred one of them serve me they have some more class) that served us was rude, arrogant, disrespectful, slow, inappropriate and idiotic. I have never in my whole life experience service like this. I was tempted to not even leave a tip because the way he was acting seemed the least we could do. We came all the way from cobble hill just to have some waiter ruin our evening. It was the topic of conversation for the next hour as we walked by the boats. I asked him a question about his menu that took him about 10 minuets to answer after checking with a woman waitress. At least he used his resources. I am not sure about you but when I pay $$$$$$$$$ per dish I expect decent service. I can get better service at a taco bell. He didnt seem to want to do anything except write the check and cash it in. I definitely recommend not visiting this establishment the service was that bad.  If for some reason you do however decide to go and try it for self do yourself a favor stay in side so you dont get served by the same waiter. You cant miss he looks like he would of been a stand in on the Jersey Shore.

Great place!
Went to the movies last night and after we went to Randazzos, it was late so they were closing, the waitress was so nice and friendly, our food came out fast but it was so good. Clams were so perfect! lots of bread and butter and I had penne pasta with chicken vodka and it was delicious, my husband had some stuffed fish and he loved it too. It was so much food that we had to packed it up. I wasn't going to have any drink but my hubby convinced me so I had a blue moon and it was just a great meal at a perfect place . 
I can't wait to go back during Summer and seat outside!
This seems like a popular local spot. The clams actually weren't that good, but the crab cakes were fantastic.

Randazzo's is one of those family places! Ive been coming here since I was a kid and my family always comes back!  The food is amazingly fresh! They shuck them right in the front of the restaurant where it's visible to the public. Amazing! I always get the Zuppa di mussels in red sauce. The sauce is amazing! Everything is good! Raw clams, pasta, steamers! The new england clam Chowder is always on point! Deliciousness!

Randazzo's reminded me of an old school local favorite, where they take pride in offering fresh and tasty seafood.  You don't go there for a nice, candle lit dinner for two.  My boyfriend and me sat at the food counter, because the place was packed!  We didn't mind, because we enjoy taking in all the action "behind the scenes".  We wanted to order pretty much everything on the menu, so it was hard to narrow down our order.  

We shared Calamari with the hot sauce, steamed little neck clams, and zuppa di mussels in white wine sauce.  Calamari was A+.  I didn't really care for the hot sauce - it had a smokey burnt flavor.  Steamed little neck clams were A+ and Zuppa di Mussels were B+.  Next time, I would have liked to try something like the crab legs or fried shrimp.  But, basically, everything coming out of the kitchen looked great!

Very expensive for nothing. Two sodas, two orders of oysters, and one order ob baked clams, $82. We had to go get pizza afterwards. I have not been there in ten years or more, I will never go back!

PS not the end of the world, but our table was dirty and the guy came over with a dirty rag to clean it. We complained about that to them too.

Extremely overpriced for the type of food you're getting - because nearly everything there is fried! Its hard to tell the quality of the seafood if its battered and basted into deep fried nonsense. Things you wouldn't expect to be fried came out fried. its ridiculous. Plus, the service is abhorrent and the concept of water pitchers with flimsy small plastic clear cups seems lazy and unsanitary. Not to mention heartburn to the max. Save you time and money and head over to city island in the bronx, where you can get quality seafood at an amazing price on top of great scenery. Perfect summer date!

I have definitely reviewed Randazzo's before but okay!

Randazzo's is a no-frill seafood/pasta place where you go to slurp oysters/clams, pour water from a bright blue pitcher, and eat either pasta or a filet.  The inside and the decor are the same as they always have been.  The staff rarely changes (the manager and the waitress both remember me each time I go).  There are tables and chairs that most would find uncomfortable.  There is also a bar area where you can go to just eat some oysters without anyone bothering you.  It's perfect and it's casual.  

We started out with a dozen oysters (as we always do).  They were extremely fresh and come with cocktail sauce, horseradish, tons of lemons, and Tabasco sauce already provided on each table.  Someone nearby had the steamed mussels and those looked absolutely delicious, as well.  For my entree, I had the filet with a baked potato on the side.  The filet was so tender and drenched in a lovely butter sauce.  They'll also give you bread for you to dunk at the end.  

The prices are a little more on the pricey side but the food is fresh so it's very much worth the cost.  You can look across the street and see where most of those fish came from.  The service is fast but not rushed.  They have lollipops at the front to grab before you depart.  The menu is basic but has something for everyone.  I love this place.  Why all the hate?

There are not a lot of Italians left in New York. It's a sad fact, but that's how cities change. Little Italy has a bunch of sub-par, overpriced Italian restaurants. Tourist shops too. Court Street has a handful of places left, Bronx too, and very few left on the Upper West Side. My understanding is that Italian tourists came here in the 1800s, made money, impacted the culture, and skipped out for the suburbs in the 60s.

So when the 60-something guy who's frantically running around behind the counter yells, "I'm-a gonna get you the calimar-a right now, hold-a your horses!" to the woman running the register, it's special. It's a living artifact of the city, that despite a rapidly evolving city, ethnic groups in and out, and hurricane freaking Sandy, maintains.

Randazzo's does two things really well: Fresh seafood and red sauce. Don't get soup. Don't get chicken. Who goes to a seafood place and gets chicken? Go with the vibe. Sitting at the counter, watching the controlled chaos, and eating the food is special. There aren't a lot of places like this any more.

And just so I talk about the food a little bit more, let me add in that the red sauce is some of the best I've ever had. Anywhere, at any price point. It tastes like it's been cooking all day, maybe longer. It's smooth, thick, zesty, spicy and awesome. The mussels are some of the best I've ever had. Shrimp and calamari were really good. And while I'm nowhere near an expert on scungili, they tasted good as well.

If I had a friend in town that wanted an authentic, delicious, old-school New York experience, Randazzo's is on the short list of where I would send them.

I was totally caught off guard by the goodness of Randazzo's. I thought the food was a bit on the expensive side, but I figured seafood isn't cheap.  Also, the portion are small, but after taking my first bite on their fried calamari I was sold.  Of course, I have to give proper credit to everything and I don't know what's on the calamari sauce, but it was so good! You can choose medium or hot and I had to get the hot sauce for myself.  It was the best decision I made because the hot sauce hit the spot for me as I ate the fried calamari.

The new england clam chowder was good, the clam in it was soft and tasty.  The chowder was creamy and delicious, however, I have to say that I've tasted creamier and tastier clam chowder.  

Service here is also exceptional, the server we got was very friendly and we didn't have any problem getting our water filled because he gave us a pitcher to fill it ourselves whenever we needed.  

I will definitely be coming back here for the fried calamari.  Unfortunately for me,  I don't know if I would be able to appreciate other fried calamaris after tasting Randazzo's. When you've tasted the best, it's hard to go back.
Cheap seafood isn't good and good seafood isn't cheap.  Randazzo's was the first place I ever had raw oysters and they were really good.  I also really enjoyed the fried calamari with spicy sauce.
This is my main place for seafood. Great food. A bit pricey, but the amount of food they give you for the money you spend is ok. Customer service could be better.

The seafood here is incredible.  Little rough around the edges but that's what you come for.  I'd be six hundred pounds if I lived closer.  Like diabetes, heart attacks, morbid obesity. it'd be worth it for the fried clams with hot sauce though.  I'd be sloppy fat.  Disgusting. The food here is that good.

For my boo's big "pay day date" he steered me down to Sheepshead Bay for an epic seafood meal. I was a little overdressed for the no-nonsense atmosphere, but I fixed that by promptly spilling red sauce all over myself as soon as the appetizer arrived.

We started with a dozen oysters, because YOLO. They were fresh and juicy, and served with cocktail sauce and a side of extra horseradish. After a year or so of slurping $1 happy hour oysters, these were a huge upgrade.

We split the sampler platter, a heaping plate of calamari, fried shrimp, steamed mussels, and scungilli. The calamari was some of the best I've had, but the shrimp was my personal fav. Big, juicy, fresh, amazing. We had the whole thing covered in spicy red sauce, which we were scooping  up with forks by the end.

We also shared the Shrimp Fra Diavallo over linguini. There were those fat, juicy, shrimp again, this time sautteed rather than fried, accompanied by mussels and clams in their shells, covered in The Sauce. The portion was huge, perfect for sharing. 

I'm pretty sure we ordered the perfect items, so when I return (I will return), I'll get "the usual."

I had high expectations going to Randazzo's as their "spicy sauce" and baked clams have been raved about by celebrity chefs and have inspired such menus as Parm and Carbone.  Randazzos's also boasts numerous accolades from various media sources as being the best seafood restaurant in New York. 
We started with the baked clams and fried calamari aka "galamar" ("can you say galamar"- the back of the wait staff's t-shirts read). Both great - although the sauce for the calamari was different than what I expected - it was a heavy tomato paste style with a lot of spice and oregano - it grew on me. The calamari were tender, large rings, fried to perfection. 
After the starters we went right into lobster fradiavolo. We shared the fradiavolo amongst 3 of us ($50) and with a side of pasta (just in case) we had more than enough, and some leftovers. The sauce was spicy as expected and full of flavor from massive chunks of garlic and herbs throughout. Yummmmmm thinking about it now is making me wish I took those last few strands of linguine home with me. 
Glad Randazzo's made it's comeback after being destroyed by Super Storm Sandy. This place is a true Italian gem. Seating is available outside (it's windy and a little chilly, even on an 85 degree day) and seems to be the less desirable choice. We were able to get a seat right away, while the inside had a wait.

I was incredibly surprised by the subpar mediocre food after my girlfriend raved about it.  Even she was shocked and said "This wasn't like this last year".  After a long day of fishing (and not catching anything), we figured this was the best place to get revenge on the eluding sea food.  Let me start of with the positive.  Our waitress Joanna was nice and very accommodating.  It wasn't her fault most of the food is terrible.  I seriously don't understand what people rave about.  Maybe it's a bad night for them?  The prices are really high for the type of food.  Pics of the food reviewed here will be posted as well.  The Cole Seafood platter was so disappointing!  It comes with 1 whole lobster, 4 raw oysters, 4 raw clams, 1 biscuit, and 2 jumbo shrimp.  First thing I tasted was the oyster...it was warm!  Then the clam and it too was warm.  The lobster was dry and literally flavorless.  It was not succulent at all.  The only thing which was passable was the shrimp cocktail....if they messed this up, god help them.  And all this for a mere market price of $55....yum

Ordered the lobster bisque.  These people do NOT know how to make good bisque.  It was served to me in room temperature (if that).  Why isn't my soup piping hot?  I told Joanna my soup is really bad and wasn't even hot.  The buss boy took my soup away and brought it out again.....reheated with the microwave....SERIOUSLY?!  Whatever, I choked down half of the bisque and didn't finish it.  it was bland and tasted more like heavy cream  than lobster.  The lobster roll ($21) was also extremely disappointing.  I have never eaten lobster so bland before....from anywhere!  (soup, sandwich, or served whole).  A little salt and / or butter goes a loooooong way!  The fried clams and fried zucchini was also just barely passable.  I don't know how this place stays in business.  Do people really just settle for sub-mediocre food and rave on Yelp?  

I need to go to Luke's in Manhattan to get my lobster roll fix.  I don't mind spending the money on food, but I do mind wasting money on terrible food.

I usually don't come to the Sheepshead Bay area, but decided to make the trip one day for some seafood. I heard this place was damaged during Sandy, but I was glad to see the place bustling when I walked in. They have outdoor seating as well. 

I started off with the lobster bisque. They put a lot of different ingredients in it, and it didn't look like lobster bisque at first, until I discovered all the delicious lobster pieces hidden at the bottom of the bowl. For my main dish, I had the shrimp randazzo with linguine. The plate was large and came with 2 clams, 2 mussels, and plenty of jumbo shrimp. There were little red peppers scattered around the linguine, giving the dish a little kick.

I'm looking forward to coming back to try more things on their menu, especially their oysters. The service here is friendly and the workers like to joke around with each other. It's a great location too; you can talk a nice walk on the strip after dinner on a breezy summer night. For an authentic Brooklyn food experience, come to Randazzo's.

I came here twice. The first time, all the food was superb. I got the New England clam chowder and a lobster with noodle dish. The lobster was cooked perfectly and even though the dish was huge for one person, I ate almost everything because it was so good.

Now, the second time was a different story. I ordered the same lobster dish, but this time it was tasteless and overcooked. I was truly disappointed, especially because you pay a good amount for it.

Food not that great! Overhyped to the max! Staff was very friendly! It's worth going for a nice day and walking around the area and the water!!! Sauce tasted like jar sauce. Maybe I am "picky" with my Italian but so is Brooklyn! I've heard it use to be better here. Whatever the case-when we went-we were NOT impressed at all with the food! Calamari was pretty good but the tomato sauce (aka gravy) ruined it!

I have been coming here for years and almost always order the same thing.  Their Lobster Fra Diavolo is AMAZING!  A whole lobster with shrimps, clams and mussels smothered in their fantastic homemade sauce with lots of fresh pieces of garlic is exquisite.  Served with a side order of perfect pasta!  
This is not a fancy place by any means (reason why i give it a 4 Star).  They bring your beer with a plastic cup, but it's all worth it when you taste the food.
Go there once and you'll keep going back for that amazing sauce!

One word.
YUM!

Sheepshead Bay? Where the heck is that? Well, if you like clams and calamari like I do, you go to the extra trouble to find out.

Do yourself a favor. If you have a spouse or significant other or even a platonic friend, shoot them an email and tell them you are taking them out for a special treat. Tell them to wear red, because they are going to be splashing red sauce everywhere and include a close up picture of a nice, juicy oyster - because that's one of the best thing they have at Randazzo's. Don't be shy, order 2 dozen to start.

My ex-girlfriend and I always came here on special days and even not so special days! LOL. We just couldn't get enough. Face it, at any other seafood place you're gonna get ripped off and probably a third of the time you're gonna get sick. At Randazzos the fish is always fresh, the kitchen is spotless (seriously, ask to see it) and the prices are right up my alley.
We drive in to Brooklyn from Long Island its a treat to do it!!  Love the Brooklyn attitude  "Cheap seafood is not fresh  Fresh seafood is not Cheap"  Love it!!

I soley came here on the recommendation of a coworker, saying that the food was simply very reminiscent of his mother's cooking, and nothing else came closer to it.  Since this man seemed to be very determined to pop my Randazzo's cherry, I decided to face the facts and see what the truth really was.  

My beau and I walked in, without reservations, and got a table in the back closest to the TV.  The waitress was all smiles and was very polite.  All walks of life walked through the front door - moms and dads, to soon-to-be's, to "we've been there, and done that".  Everyone seems welcome here, and the regulars have their designated seats.

We started with the clam chowder, and that was hearty, with a piece of clam in every bite!  It was seasoned well, and didn't taste fishy or diner-like; this was a fisherman's soup!  Really worth a taste!

For the main event, I opted for the crab cake sandwich, and boyfriend got the Fisherman's platter.  My crab cake sandwich was colossal and my beau's platter was even larger!  The plates are definitely packed on without hesitation, and were meant to fill you up if you didn't bother to eat at all that day.  

So, why the three stars?  Unfortunately for us, this turned out to be one of those places that it's all good going down, but reeked havoc the next day.  We still can't determine to this day if it was the infamous dipping sauce, or how they fried the food.  

Sadly, we aren't too brave to come back in the very near future.

[Update]: I've since had to change my review from 4-stars to 3-stars, when seeing that my boyfriend was charged $37 for a $15 t-shirt, a lobster bisque, and a clam chowder. Apparently there are 2 sets of prices - 1 for stay-in and one for take-out, which isn't listed anywhere in the store, or on any online menus. The prices for take-out orders are $2 more per item. So we were charged $11 for lobster bisque (now not really worth it for the price), and $8 for the clam chowder (barely worth it). Man, this is horrible. I've always loved Randazzo's - as my review shows, but this is really shady business dealings! Sad. 

Now my original review before being duped...


I love Randazzo's! 

The lobster bisque is pretty solid (sometimes lacking on the salt - but made up for when you add a dash of some, or add a package of oyster crackers). Not an overwhelming lobster taste, but smooth, and clean. I sometimes feel it's missing just a little something, but can never quite pinpoint what that is. But don't get me wrong, it's good!

The clam chowder is FANTASTIC! Thick, creamy, hearty, with at least a clam in every bite - they definitely don't skimp! Some of my favorite, anywhere. 

Their fried calamari is tender, melt-in-your mouth deliciousness. And the marinara it comes with is equally tasty. Good thing I was wearing a red t-shirt, because it got everywhere, and I don't have a single complaint about that.

My only issue with Randazzo's is that their prices are kinda on the steep side. But as the sign there says "good seafood isn't cheap, and cheap seafood isn't good."

I'm a HUGE oyster fan, and I've had their oysters before and they're great, but when I pay $1 per oyster in the city, I'd be pretty hard pressed to drop the $24 for a dozen that they charge here. But if money  isn't an issue for you, go at it! Their cherrystone and Little Neck clams are equally fresh and delicious at $15/dozen.

The bisque will set you back $9 for a bowl, the chowder $6, and the fried calamari $14. 

They're never overly crowded, but never dead either. The atmosphere is incredibly casual and no-nonsense. 

The workers there are sweethearts - both the individuals behind the counter as well as the servers, and especially the guy over the phone taking orders. Never had a problem, and they've always been helpful with questions. And the servers bring you your orders quickly and efficiently, but you never feel rushed out, which is nice. Their kitchen is also incredibly clean, which has always been a big deal for me, and something you've gotta appreciate. 

And there's nothing like ordering take out and taking a lovely stroll along the bay across the street to watch the swans at sunset while eating really delicious seafood. 

And best of all they have my "Can You Say Galamah?" t-shirt that I love so dearly.
 
Every time I have my heart set on returning it's always to try something new - like their crab cakes - but I somehow always end up getting the chowder and calamari that I love so dearly. Next time, though! I'll veer from my usuals! I promise you, Yelp! And review accordingly!

When Hurricane Sandy passed through I was heartbroken to see that Randazzo's suffered so much damage, and I hoped (and prayed) that they'd find a way to recover. I'm so glad that they have, and are back in the swing of things. Randazzo's is a Sheepshead Bay institution since 1932. It's one of the few places on Emmons Ave. that still exist from my childhood (along with Roll N Roaster). It's nice to know that they're still around, and that they ain't going nowhere! (and thank goodness for that)

Would I come back here? Of course, it's Randazzo's!
Calamari was way too expensive for the small portion, food and service were ok, I don't understand the hype about this place, maybe it used to be good, but not anymore.

I came here because I heard about the famous seafood here. I have to admit the food was good but not the best especially with that price. I will not be coming back again unless someone else is paying for my meal. The calamari  was not so good, the sauce however was great. Crab cake is pretty big and good , but i would have prefer some homemade tarter sauce not package ones. Mt favorite was the soup , the spicy corn and crab soup?? It was great but still not worth that much money. I also had the pasta with vodka sauce and shrimp, it was okay the shrimp does taste fresh but the pasta was okay. Overall the food is okay not that crazy over it, I wanted to order a lobster but not for 35 dollars!!! I can easily order a fresh lobster in another restaurant for much less. It was just overprice no matter how fresh it is.  Fresh lobster is like 4 dollars a pound at the supermarket for 35 dollars i can get a lot of them and steam it my self, and most Chinese restaurant serve lobster for around 20 dollars ( some for around 10)  and is usually two lobsters so..... Nope is not worth it. I would recommend this restaurant for its seafood's freshness but for that ridiculous price.

Nope. Nope. Nope.

Frozen food, rare server sightings, rude attitudes, and an up-charge to sit outside on their metal picnic tables featuring a fantastic view of the side-street where cars park (the water is around the corner and across the street).

This is not even to mention that the messed up my order. Not a big problem for me except that having them correct it would've taken time I just did not want to spend in that place. I considered it punishment for wanting to go there in the first place. Lesson learned. 

Boo.

Local place for me within waling distance which my dad has gotten take out from here since i was a little kid. I went here last night & the calamari was as amazing as possible. YOU HAVE TO GET THE FRIED CALAMARI with HOT SAUCE!!! 

"It's all about the sauce" & it is true. Every sauce they have is AMAZING! 

Tried the Rigatoni with Vodka sauce last night for the first time. It was DELICIOUS! Friend got the red clam sauce & it was DELICIOUS too! 

This is the Brooklyn that I know, that I grew up with. This is the Old Brooklyn that I hope never disappears. Love Randazzo's!

The quintessential Brooklyn italian American old school red sauce joint (not fancy). Service is good food is good! Can u say galamah (calamari!!!). Lobster Dra diavolo is worth it and good flavor. Lobster bisque is one of the best not creamy or gooky! Enjoy it! And wear your bib!

The food is ok.  The prices are astronomical for this type of place and setting though, they easily charge twice as much as similar places with food that is just as good.  The outdoor area needs improvement as well, it's a bunch of metal tables/benches, the kind you see in public parks - and it's facing a busy parking garage.

Let me start with this they are extremely over priced!! I did enjoy there oysters and the sauce that comes with it, the house wine is not even worth it, the mussels tasted good, the fried calamari was ok I've actually tasted better and the stuffed little neck clams Did not impress me all that much, I know every restaurant has a there good days and bad but dam 174.00  for 5-6 dishes was crazy the place just looks like a cheap dinner yet there prices are sky rocket  high the portions are so small I must add for 4 adults and 1 child 3 beers 174.. Was way to much I feel like I got robbed. And the food wasn't that amazing absolutely disappointed wont go back!

After a long, hot day at Coney Island, I headed over to Sheepshead Bay for the first time to Randazzo's, and it was worth the visit.  Among the things I ordered were the Spicy Crab Corn Chowder, raw oysters, and their platter of steamed mussels and scungilli and fried shrimp and calarmari in a spicy sauce.  5 stars for all of it.  The sauce is truly delicious and had a nice kick.  The calamari was probably the star of the meal.  Easy laid back family atmosphere, right across from the water.  Very good way to end a summer's day.  Definitely will be back.

Best Mussels in Brooklyn!

We have been going to Randazzo's for 16 years. We always order the Zuppa di Mussels  (red sauce - not the white). It is so delicious. I haven't tried the other items on Randazzo's menu because I always order the mussels. The waitress brings a large white bowl filled with the mussels and the delicious marinara sauce - OMG so good!  Everyone who works at Randazzo's is fantastic. The waitresses are always personable, polite and just nice people. Paul, the owner actually cares about his business and walks around the restaurant to speak with customers and ask if they like the food. He did this 16 years ago when I first started coming to Randazzo's and he did it yesterday (Sept. 4, 2013). 

Paul's mother (God rest her soul) worked in the restaurant too and was a lovely lady. 

Are the prices high - they are competitive with other restaurants in Brooklyn who don't have fresh seafood. If you are looking for a good Seafood place with a casual atmosphere, try Randazzo's. You will keep going back just like us.  BTW, make sure to get the mints on the way out. They are just part of the experience - so good.

I've been coming here since the '60s.  Can the servers be rude at time? You bet. Overpriced? Oh Yeah! The best Calamari you'll have in life, EVER? YES!!!!    It's the sauce. Once they get to know you, they treat you like family. Pauly will stop what he's doing to come over and say hi. If you've never been here you have to try it. It's worth the trip. Oh, if your going to order the Calama, order it like that. CA LA MA, not calamari, everyone will look at you funny.

I must say the Lobster Fra Diavolo is pretty amazing even at the "market price" of $49.50. Big lobster with a ton of shrimp, mussels and clams over pasta. The sauce is delicious with just the right amount of heat and the fish is fresh. Best I've had. Casual "old school" place that's all about the consistent quality of delicious food more than anything else.

The only reason this isn't five stars is because, as other reviewers have said, it is a little pricey for what you get.  That would be the only real downside I experienced, but still, I'd do it again, anyway.  It was a shellfish lover's paradise for me and my beau - we started with the shrimp cocktail and a half dozen raw oysters.  We added on some baked clams (10 littlenecks) and finished up with the zuppa di mussels in red sauce, which was to die for!  We would have ordered something else, but the sauce the mussels were in was so good, we were surprised we were not given any bread to go with it.  So I called our waitress and asked for some.  She smiled and informed me they had run out, but just sent their boy to the store to get more, so if we just hold tight... less than 10 minutes later a basket of bread was out.  We wound up asking for a second basket because we wanted as much of that sauce as possible, and after all that we were stuffed!  

Overall, an excellent experience and I would definitely go back!

Good food but very over priced for what it is. I had the raw oysters, fried calamari, raw clams, and the seafood pasta. 

This place has been around for a very long time and the decor appears to be a bit run down. I came here on a Friday night and it was packed. I waited for about 10 minutes before being seated. Staff were ok- not very friendly but on point.  

It taste very fresh and obviously that's important for seafood. I also enjoyed the sauce that the food came with. Will come back here.

I went to this establishment since I heard so many good things about it. Boy, were they wrong. The service was bad, the $36 crab legs weren't seasoned/cooked properly and drinks came in a small plastic cup, like the ones you get at the dentists office. Worst of all, after I left, the food got me sick! I was unable to hold anything down the rest of the night. All I can say is this will be my first and last time attending this establishment.

This place is a fixture on Emmons Ave I have been told by many that this is a great place. I was terribly disappointed. I had Linguine with white clam sauce. It was as average as can be. For two people the bill was $ 150.00. We had jug wine in single serve bottles. When I asked for a glass of water I was presented with a small plastic dixie cup. I was told it's a clam bar not really a full service restaurant. She was right and I will never go there again. My friend had Seafood Fra Diavolo. It too was average. Sorry can't recommend this one. The staff was pleasant and friendly and I think agreeing with my consternation about everything!

To all those who responded to this review.
I had Linguine with White Cam sauce at Randazzo's,  It was just mediocre. Try Don Peppe's on Lefferts Blvd in Ozone Park. You will never go back to Randazzo's. Don Peppe's uses cherry stone clams and they are Fresh and Delicious. It is Sicilian style so love garlic or go home! It was even better when the father ran it but it is still worth the trip it is the best in NYC PERIOD. Try their baked clams. In dishes like these the quality of the olive oil is paramount just as the freshness of the clams. Go there and then write me and tell me that Randazzo's is better or even half as good. Also, don't talk about fried fish. If a seafood restaurant can't fry fish well. they don't belong in business. And $ 150.00 for two people in a clam bar is ridiculous. But I don't care about the money. The rest of the food at Don Peppe's is competent but not my fav.
Sorry Francesco M.

Made a reservation and did not get seated until 30 mins later. Poor service and no manner; what is the purpose of making reservation when you have to wait 30mins? 

Seafood is average but the price is above average, makes this place not worth going. 

Two stars, I had fun with my friends and for not rushing me 

I will spend my cash somewhere else where I get treated like a customer

My absolute favorite place to eat. Well worth the hour drive from home.  I try and come as often as possible.  I love it here. If it's your first time here then you must try the fried calamari, baked clams, lobster bisque, spicy crab corn chowder and a minimum of 2 dozen raw oysters before your main course which I recommend to be the fra diavlo lol that is if you can handle an amazing dinner. Wow what a meal.
I just don't get it. Ok food, nothing special. Very arrogant service. Very fresh seafoods but the recipes should be rethought. Waitresses are authentic and rude

It really doesn't get any more authentic BK than this.   My parents have been going there since years before they had me.  Actually, I've been going there since I was eating in a highchair.  This place was severely damaged in Sandy and underwent a total kitchen renovation and all Bk rejoiced when they reopened.   The service is straightforward and quick, the owner is friendly and so glad to see you.  There are tons of regulars.  One thing not to miss is their marinara sauce --- plain (not spicy), mild or hot.   It's perfect over their sidedish-sized pasta and especially over the fried calamari.  Also, the best lobster roll in town. Humongous and a total bargain at $20, since it has about a pound of fresh lobster tail dressed very lightly and simply.  I don't understand why anyone would think this place is expensive... try having a lobster roll, clam chowder, bowl of mussels anywhere else in the popular areas of Brooklyn and I guarantee you, you will pay way more.   Not to be missed here: grilled swordfish, pasta with vodka sauce and shrimp, clam chowder, crab and corn chowder (my fave!), pasta with clams and the oysters.  MMMM!
Amazing food. Was there a few days ago and lovedddddd the shrimp far diavlo!!! Calamari were good as well. The only thing that they lack is good service because they are very nasty and rude!

I have been coming here for over 15 years for one reason only... The New England Clam Chowder. I've made several trips to Maine and tried NE chowder all over the east coast and had dozens of bowls from all over the place but nothing beats this place. In my opinion you won't find a better, creamier, meatier chowder anywhere around here. 

I haven't really explored too much on the menu since prices are pretty steep for most of the bigger entree's, although I do like ordering the fried clams occasionally. As the sign says, "good seafood isn't cheap, cheap seafood isn't good". Quality product is something I've never really questioned about this place. 

The staff are great and it's nice when you recognize the same faces year after year. A true family owned business. Definitely worth a visit if your a seafood fan but don't expect this to be a cheap meal.

A lady friend  and I went here on a Friday night around 8:30 and were seated immediately which I was pretty happy about. Pretty bright place as far as lighting goes, and dress codes don't exist. Very old school in an 80's way as far as decor goes. Looked like a place you'd see in Goodfellas. 

The service was pretty sub par as far as waitressing went. There were 4 or 5 waitresses all sitting at a table talking together the whole time. Our waitress wasn't paying attention to us at all. Even when our food was ready, someone from the kitchen had to come out and yell at her to get up and get it. She's probably a family member who really doesn't care about doing a good job to be honest. The bus boys walked around the whole time taking plates and bottles as they were finished. They did an excellent job, and we actually tipped our main bus boy separately. 

Beer selection is far from amazing, but they have most of the "basics" and all at $5 a bottle (no beers on tap). They also have a few different wines. 

The food was very very good. Honestly good enough for the service and beer selection to be weak, and still able to merit 5 stars. 

We started with the Lobster bisque and it was great. Very creamy, nice pieces of lobster chunks in it, all around great. 

We also got the calamari as an appetizer.  Not "the best in the world" as some others have said, but definitely didn't disappoint at all. It only comes with a side of marinara though, no tarter or white sauce. 

My girlfriend got the chicken francese and said it was great. I didn't try it so I can't say too much about it. Sorry. 

I got the rigatoni with vodka sauce and chicken, and it was one of the best pasta dishes (or any dish) I've ever had. Very big portion, heavy creamy thick sauce, and a ton of flavor. I felt stupid for not getting a seafood entree, but then once I tried it I knew I had made the right choice. 

For all the people who said its pricey, I do agree, but it wasn't nearly as bad as I thought. For the cup of lobster bisque, calamari, chicken francese, rigatoni vodka with chicken, and a Heineken, the bill came to about $63. I went expecting to drop at least $80, so I was happy. 


Overall: amazing food, relaxed environment, mediocre waitressing, and definitely worth the trip!

Long standing establishment.  I could feel the homey aspect of it. Staff was wonderful and attentive.  To me the food was average. Didn't really eat anything that stood out. Had the fried squid and crab cakes.

My go-to seafood place in Brooklyn! It's close by my house, parking is never too difficult, never a long wait for a table. What more can a girl ask for? :D

Now food wise - I LOVE lobster so I almost always get the Lobster Fra Diavolo with Linguini. Of course, I have to share because I can never ever finish it. SO yummy and love that it comes with other shellfish besides the lobster.

I've never tried much of anything else ..... because I like to stick to one item and I hate change. :)

Looking forward to coming back and then MAYBE I'll try new items!

Oh and it would be nice to walk the strip after dinner but its so smelly in that area so there goes that romantic idea.

Amazing Seafood spot.
Casual atmosphere.
Best raw clams & shellfish i have ever had.
New England clam chowder right on the money.
OMG_ The Fried Calamari- lightly breaded, fresh fried, and with by far the best red sauce you will ever have. Medium or Hot sauce, both are ridiculously good- thick, tasty, yummy, unbelievable sauce.
The linguini shrimp fra diavlo was prepared perfectly and a good size portion.
Basically all food in this place is top notch.
Highly recommend this place to everyone.
Side note: best service is at the bar- Emil or Pauly will take good care of you!

what a waste I went there with friends.   we were seated by what looked like a dishwasher . we ordered shrimp cocktail and some were still with the vein.  there was some one who acted like ralphie from the sopranos..  I understand the level of service is hampered by the motif of a clam bar but for goodness sake the pastas were par boiled and the portions were small.  the ladies were pleasant and helpful. i wont disparage. when its not deserved.  its definitely overpriced and honestly some pizza restaurants  on long island make really great food that randazzos wished upon a star it could.  the web site says we use gulf shrimp right i drove 40 minutes to eat   here and those aren't gulf shrimp.  this was the first and definitely the last. how I miss  lundys

This place rocks for seafood! My favorite dishes are the shrimp and the scungili smothered in medium sauce. Their fried zucchinis are delicious too. The ambiance is nice and the staff are down to earth, a real pleasure to talk to. I give this place 2 thumbs up!!!

I am writing this review and I am overqualified to do so. I could also be biased but I don't care. I can't fathom anyone loving seafood and NOT loving Randazzo's. 

Can't remember the first time I was here, nor can I recall how many times I've stepped foot in this place. The number is probably staggering. 

The seafood, CONSISTENTLY, is cooked/fried perfectly. The true taste of everything you order stands on its own. No heavy seasoning needed. Even the french fries are great. 

And the real gold here.....The sauce! You not beat this sauce, you couldn't even come close to duplicating it either. So don't bother.  

This isn't for you fancy suit and tie folk, this is for the foodies. Great staff, great service, great food. you really can't beat it. 

All hail Scuniglli with hot sauce.

This place is a great place to go to. Pleasant waitresses and waiters. Always asking if we need anything taking out plates and giving us clean ones. The food was delicious lobster melts in your mouth. Even something simple as a salad was delicious with fresh vegetables. Recommend this place to anyone who wants great seafood in a local and friendly spot.

One look at the menu and I swore I had died and gone straight to deep-fried hell.  I'm not big into consuming mass quantities of Crisco, but my friends insisted that we go during my time in NY.  What appeared on my plate, however, was some grease-soaked monstrosity of a dinner that left me with little more than a thinner wallet and a clogged toilet.  Won't be going back.
Been there many times through the years...still the best seafood! Come from long island just to go there...excellent lobster,calamari. .the best mussels marinara...besides mine of course!

VERY fresh seafood, but also VERY expensive.  Service isn't all that great, it takes a while to get your food and sometimes difficult to get the waiter/waitress' attention.  I'm not sure what's up with the stale hard piece of bread with soggy exterior that they put on your plate but all the other food is delicious.  I'd definitely come back.  I'll add this note - if you're looking to eat healthy this might not be the best choice.

Not sure what your looking for but i think this place is perfect no frills place. this is not a hipster place. you come here becuase you want fresh seafood and thats what they have. my boy had the calamari. it was tender and a decent size portion we split the new england clam chowder. it was tasty. i had the scungilli in hot. the hot is not to hot and it was tasty. the did see the massive seafood pasta dishes and some tasty looking seafood sandwiches. maybe next time we head over to coney island we go there for dinner again.

When that seafood crave comes around, my only go to place is here. Love this place!
My ritual start with a bowl of soup, mixed lobster bisque and spicy corn, then work my way to some steamers. Catch it on a season and theses steamers are plump, creamy and juicy. Finish with fried galamah and hot sauce on it with a side of spaghetti marinara.
